relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED against the document's own front matter and against the registered entry's volume/issue/article-number. Citation is heavily load-bearing in `rem:schrodinger-color-falsifiability` — and TWO of the claims made there are NOT supported by the source. (1) MISCITED — FABRICATED CROSSOVER. `schrodinger-color-falsifiability.md:41` writes: 'Bujack et al. found the diminishing-returns effect barely significant at Δd = 5 (β=0.048, p=0.010) and strongly significant at Δd = 10 (β=0.119, p<0.001). The perceptual crossover empirically lies in [5,10], bracketing the predicted d* ≈ 9.6.' Both numbers are quoted correctly from Table 1 (p. 5) — but they are the regression coefficients on the Δd INDICATOR LEVELS, i.e. how much larger a Δd=10 stimulus pair is judged than the baseline. They rise with Δd under ANY monotone metric, including a purely Riemannian one, so they carry no information about a Riemannian→logarithmic crossover. The source's diminishing-returns coefficient is the SEPARATE β_d̄ = −0.005, a single number that is not a function of Δd. The source reports NO crossover scale anywhere. The 'empirical crossover in [5,10] bracketing d* ≈ 9.6' is therefore an artifact of misreading the regression — and it is the only numerical corroboration the block offers for η. (2) OVERSTATED — 'proved'. Line 5 of the block says the source 'proved that perceived color differences violate Riemannian additivity'. The source explicitly hedges the very coefficient at issue (p. 5): the β_d̄ result 'relies on the L* axis being nearly perceptually uniform. This assumption may not be appropriate, so we interpret the negativity of the β_d̄ as WEAKLY SUPPORTING our claim of nonadditivity and as motivation to carry out further analysis.' (3) STATUS INFLATION in the Table 3 data block: the second-order Weber–Fechner row is marked '✓' under 'Empirical status', but the source calls it a conjecture — 'Our findings HINT at the potential existence of a second-order Weber–Fechner law… More research must go into the validation of this conjecture' (p. 8). WHAT IS CORRECT: every Table-1 figure is quoted exactly (β₀=0.161/t=8.894; β_{Δd=5}=0.048/t=2.815/p=0.010; β_{Δd=10}=0.119/t=6.632; β_d̄=−0.005/t(60)=−5.566; R²=0.556, F(3,60)=25.00); the sub-additivity direction ΔE(A,C) < ΔE(A,B)+ΔE(B,C) matches the source's diminishing-returns finding; the ~0.5 power-law exponent attribution to prior suprathreshold work matches p. 3. Verdict is `supporting` not `core`: the source genuinely supplies the qualitative non-Riemannian / sub-additive fact the block needs, and supplies none of the quantitative agreement the block claims from it. Separate minor item: the block evaluates at q₀ ≈ 1.109978595554181, which matches NEITHER documented pin (proton 1.1099785827513808, muon 1.10997859555733471) — it diverges from the muon value at the 11th decimal.

keyResults.statement: The authors interpret the negativity of β_d̄ as WEAKLY supporting nonadditivity, conditional on the L* axis being nearly perceptually uniform — an assumption they say 'may not be appropriate'.
keyResults.useForFolio: Downgrades the block's 'proved' to 'reported evidence for'.

relevance.rationale: Reinterprets Milnor's triple linking number mu-bar(ijk) of a 3-component sub-link as a Seifert-surface count: mu-bar(ijk) = m(F) - t(F) mod delta, where t(F) is the signed count of triple points of three Seifert surfaces in general position, m(F) is a Magnus-coefficient sum read off the double-point words on the boundaries, and delta is the gcd of the three pairwise linking numbers. It generalises the classical 'algebraic count of triple points' formula, which the paper recovers as the special case where the pairwise linkings vanish (the Brunnian/baryon regime the corpus works in). The corpus already runs a substantial mu-bar program: MilnorIndeterminacyGate.lean encodes exactly the same mod-delta indeterminacy (ZMod (gcd) residue; ZMod 1 subsingleton on a Hopf-linked spectator, ZMod 0 = Z on a Brunnian triple), the Magnus route is implemented in computations/deltalambda (binding_mn_milnor_linking / mixed_multibond_mubar_integrality_probe), and docs/audits/2026-07-11-gap2-borromean-triple-count.md localises the 3-body term M3(K) as the mu-bar-irreducible triple count. It is NOT load-bearing: the corpus computes mu-bar by Magnus expansion on braid words and has no Seifert-surface layer, so nothing here is currently consumed. Recorded as a scope-(a) reading: this document, as read, adds an alternate route and a corroborating derivation of the mod-delta convention, not a result that closes anything open.

keyResults.statement: For any choice of Seifert surfaces F for three components, mu-bar(ijk) = m(ijk)(F) - t(ijk)(F) mod delta, and one may choose F making either t(F) = 0 or m(F) = 0 mod delta.

relevance.rationale: Directly on QOU's subject matter (q-deformed polylogarithms) but with a DIFFERENT deformation: Schlesinger uses Li_{n_1..n_m}(z;q) = sum z^k/(1-q^k)^n, and says explicitly that this differs from the Kirillov/Koornwinder deformations usually discussed. That is a sharp question to ask of QOU's Li_2^q, which the corpus tags 'hopf-algebra' at rem:q-dilog-three-contexts without establishing any algebra structure.

relevance.rationale: Two corpus blocks rest on a Plancherel central limit theorem and neither cites one. conj:jet-convergence-classical-limit states 'the Kerov q-hook walk and the Feray-Meliot q-Plancherel Central Limit Theorem ensure O(1/sqrt(k)) convergence' with cites: [feray2010, kerov1996]; prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton clause (2) states 'character fluctuations have variance O(1/sqrt(n-3))' citing feray2010 alone. This document is the canonical complete proof of the q = 1 statement those blocks are deforming, written by Kerov's collaborators from his notes. It is the result the corpus's q-deformed claims are the deformation of, and the current citation does not support the claim made. Flagging the mis-citation is itself a finding.

keyResults.statement: Kerov's CLT: for lambda drawn from Plancherel measure M_n, the rescaled boundary satisfies n^{-1/2} lambda(sqrt(n) x) ~ Omega(x) + (2/sqrt(n)) Delta(x), with Omega(x) = (2/pi)(x arcsin(x/2) + sqrt(4 - x^2)) on |x| <= 2 and Delta a generalized Gaussian process given by the random trigonometric series Delta(2 cos theta) = (1/pi) sum_{k>=2} (xi_k/sqrt(k)) sin(k theta), xi_k i.i.d. standard normal.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the actual q = 1 fluctuation theorem — including the exact 1/sqrt(n) scale — that conj:jet-convergence-classical-limit's O(1/sqrt(k)) claim and prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton clause (2) are asserting a q-analogue of. relevance.rationale: QOU's rem:knot-complement-group introduces representations rho: pi_1(S^3 \ K) -> PSL(2,C) and asserts that 'the image of rho characterises the geometric structure on the knot complement' — an informal claim with no source. prop:thurston-volume-additivity computes volume by summing over an ideal triangulation, and the mass pipeline repeatedly invokes Mostow rigidity to argue the volume (hence the mass) is discrete. Francaviglia proves the rigorous cusped-manifold versions of all three: vol(rho) is well-defined for any representation, is computed by straightening any ideal triangulation, is bounded by the relative simplicial volume, and — the rigidity theorem — equals vol(M) only for the discrete faithful rho. It is background/technique that upgrades informal claims to sourced ones, not a result any QOU derivation currently needs: QOU works with the geometric representation only, where classical Thurston/Mostow already suffice.

keyResults.statement: For a cusped orientable 3-manifold M and any rho: pi_1(M) -> Isom^+(H^3), all pseudo-developing maps give the same volume (so vol(rho) is well-defined), and vol(rho) equals the straightened volume — i.e. it can be computed by straightening ANY ideal triangulation of M and summing tetrahedron volumes.
keyResults.useForFolio: prop:thurston-volume-additivity asserts triangulation-independent additivity of volume over an ideal triangulation; Thm 4.10 is the theorem that licenses 'any triangulation' in the cusped, representation-valued setting rather than only for the complete structure.

keyResults.statement: |vol(rho)| < v_3 * ||(M, dM)|| for every representation, where v_3 is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume and ||(M, dM)|| the relative simplicial (Gromov) volume.
keyResults.useForFolio: atom-knot-mass-derivation-proof invokes Gromov's norm theorem alongside Mostow in the 'post-Archimedean naming' step; Thm 5.1 is the sharp representation-level inequality in that pairing and is a citable bound on how large a non-geometric representation's volume can be.

keyResults.statement: If M is hyperbolic and vol(rho) = vol(M), then rho is discrete and faithful.
keyResults.useForFolio: This is the precise form of rem:knot-complement-group's unsourced claim that 'the image of rho characterises the geometric structure': volume maximality singles out the geometric representation. relevance.rationale: Defines the extended Bloch group Bhat(C), proves lambda : H_3(PSL(2,C)^delta; Z) -> Bhat(C) is an isomorphism, and shows the extended Rogers dilogarithm Rhat descends so that R o lambda is the Cheeger--Chern--Simons class, i(vol + i cs) in C/pi^2 Z. Two distinct corpus artifacts depend on precisely this and neither cites it. (1) docs/audits/2026-08-07-extended-bloch-group-fixes-the-normalization-fit.md (dated one day before this triage, PR #4664) builds its whole argument on 'the extended Bloch group is the canonical resolution of the branch-of-logarithm ambiguity' and even quotes Rhat(betahat(M)) = Vol + i CS; the audit itself notes the phrase 'extended Bloch' occurs in exactly one corpus file. (2) conj:borromean-bloch-group-element states as a CONJECTURE that the Borromean rings complement determines a non-trivial Bloch-group element whose regulator is Vol(B_3) = 8G. Its hypotheses -- complete, finite-volume, hyperbolic 3-manifold -- hold for the Borromean complement (two ideal regular octahedra, volume 8G), so Sec. 1 and Sec. 14 of this document supply the existence, and non-triviality follows because the regulator is non-zero. keyResults.statement: Any complete hyperbolic 3-manifold of finite volume carries a natural fundamental class in H_3(PSL(2,C); Z) determining an element betahat(M) in the extended Bloch group, and R o lambda computes the Cheeger--Chern--Simons class i(vol(M) + i cs(M)).

relevance.rationale: The corpus asserts, in rem:quantum-bloch-group-framework-connection, that 'the regulator map B(q) -> R sends the algebraic volume to the hyperbolic volume' -- an unsourced claim in a remark block. This paper is the rigorous version of that statement on the A-polynomial curve: it uses the Beilinson-Deligne regulator to show the symbol {l,m} in K_2(C(Y)) is torsion for every component Y of the A-polynomial zero locus of a hyperbolic knot, and derives a quantization of the Chern-Simons period. Supporting rather than core because QOU's Bloch-group content is q-deformed and Hecke-traced, and no QOU number is computed from Li-Wang; the paper supplies the classical statement the q-deformed one is modelled on.

keyResults.statement: The closed real 1-form eta(l,m) = log|l| d arg m - log|m| d arg l is EXACT on Y_h; and for any loop gamma in Y_h, (1/4pi^2) times the integral of (log|m| d log|l| + arg l d arg m) equals k/N where N is the ORDER of the symbol {l,m} in K_2(C(Y)).
keyResults.useForFolio: Makes rigorous the corpus's 'regulator sends algebraic volume to hyperbolic volume' assertion, and supplies the quantization statement that docs/scope/2026-07-12-mq0-unified-boundary-selection.md gestures at ('a quantization condition' on the Im V = 0 locus) with no source. The torsion order N is a concrete arithmetic invariant of the A-polynomial curve that the folio's regulator language currently lacks.

keyResults.statement: The class r(l,m) in H^1(Y_h, C*) is a flat line bundle -- the pullback of the universal Heisenberg line bundle over C* x C* -- and the derived 1-form is its Chern-Simons secondary class; the generalized volume conjecture is reformulated via this 1-form.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the A-polynomial curve a K-theoretic/line-bundle structure, which is the classical shadow of what the folio calls the quantum Bloch group. Cite where def:quantum-bloch-group motivates the regulator.

keyResults.statement: The correlation between the three-body ground-state energy and the four-body ground and excited state energies is a universal curve (a Tjon line): approximately linear outside the threshold region, with positive curvature for a > 0 and negative curvature for a < 0.

relevance.rationale: computations/one_loop_torsion.py opens by documenting a LIVE disagreement between three in-repo implementations of the adjoint torsion of 4_1: sqrt(3) (declared non-invariant), sqrt(3)/2 (declared correct, = Dimofte-Garoufalidis' own worked example), and 3 (labelled 'Porti convention'). This paper computes the SL2(C) non-abelian (adjoint) Reidemeister torsion of every twist knot at the holonomy, in closed form, with published tables -- an independent external value for exactly the object the corpus is arguing about, including the whole twist-knot family rather than just 4_1. It also expresses the torsion as a rational function of the CUSP SHAPE via u = 4/(c-2), which ties the corpus's cusp-shape work (prop:cusp-shape-bar-parity) to its torsion work through an explicit substitution. This is the highest-leverage of the knot-theory papers in this slice.

keyResults.statement: The non-abelian Reidemeister torsion at the holonomy is 3 for J(2,2) (the trefoil) and -3 for J(2,-2) (the figure-eight), each up to the sign tau_0.
keyResults.useForFolio: An external published value to run against computations/one_loop_torsion.py's three-way disagreement. NOTE the normalisation carefully: DHY compute T^K_lambda, the torsion with respect to the LONGITUDE, while the corpus's '3' is labelled T_mu (meridian, Porti convention) -- so this is a cross-check to run, not an automatic adjudication. Whether the mu- and lambda-normalised values coincide for 4_1 is exactly the question the check answers.

keyResults.statement: Closed formula for T^{J(2,+-2m)}_lambda(rho_u) as an explicit rational expression in u, m and xi_+- (roots of the Cayley-Hamilton recursion for the commutator w = [y, x^{-1}]).
keyResults.useForFolio: Extends the torsion check off the single 4_1 datum to a whole one-parameter family, which is what the corpus's one_loop_torsion.py needs to distinguish a normalisation constant from a genuine invariant -- a constant factor discrepancy shows up identically across the family, a formula error does not.

keyResults.statement: For a hyperbolic two-bridge knot, the cusp shape is c = n - 2*w_{1,2}*w_{2,2}; and via u = 4/(c-2) the torsion at the holonomy is a rational function of the cusp shape c.
keyResults.useForFolio: A published cusp-shape convention (Fact 4: mu -> [[1,1],[0,1]], lambda -> [[-1,c],[0,-1]]) that the corpus should check prop:cusp-shape-bar-parity against -- that block calls omega = e^{i*pi/3} 'the cusp shape of 4_1', which is the regular ideal tetrahedron shape parameter, whereas DHY's c is the cusp-torus modulus. These are different objects and the corpus uses the same phrase for both; worth resolving before either is cited outward.

keyResults.statement: As m -> infinity the cusp shapes of J(2,+-2m) converge to 2 + 2i, the cusp shape of the Whitehead link, and |T^{J(2,-2m)}_lambda(rho_0)| grows like C*m^3.

relevance.rationale: This paper supplies a triangulation-independent computation of exactly the quantity whose triangulation-dependent computation the corpus REFUTED last week. computations/whitehead_c_sigma_torsion.py derives |tau_adjoint(L5a1)| from Neumann-Zagier ideal-triangulation data as |det J|, and carries a header note: 'REFUTED 2026-08-07 (PR #4691, bean qou-fl4t). |det J| as computed here is NOT a topological invariant: retriangulating the same manifold gives 8 distinct values for 5_2, 17 for 6_2, 6 for L5a1, 7 for L6a4.' Dubois-Yamaguchi compute the SAME adjoint (non-abelian) Reidemeister torsion by Fox free differential calculus on a Wirtinger presentation plus a derivative formula — a CW/cut-and-paste construction with no ideal triangulation anywhere, hence manifestly retriangulation-immune. And their two worked examples (§4) are precisely QOU's two anchor manifolds: the figure-eight knot exterior (the |tau(4_1)| = sqrt(3) calibration the refuted script used) and the Whitehead link exterior (= L5a1, the c_sigma = 2^{-3/4} target). The corpus already carries the 1-loop = adjoint-torsion literature (garoufalidis-yoon2024, ohtsuki-takata, dimofte-garoufalidis) but nothing giving a computational route; this is that route, and it is unregistered.

keyResults.statement: For a hyperbolic M with b torus boundary components satisfying (A_M), (A_phi), (A_rho), lim_{t->1} Delta^{phi (x) Ad.rho}_M(t) / prod_{l=1..b}(t^{a_l} - 1) = (-1)^b * T^lambda_M(rho), i.e. the derivative of the twisted Alexander invariant at t = 1 computes the non-abelian (adjoint) Reidemeister torsion for the multi-longitude lambda — for LINK exteriors, not only knot exteriors.
keyResults.useForFolio: A route to |tau_adjoint(L5a1)| that does not pass through an ideal triangulation, replacing the |det J| construction refuted in bean qou-fl4t. The multi-component (b > 1) generality is the part that matters: the earlier corpus work needed the Whitehead link (b = 2) and would need the Borromean rings (b = 3) next.

relevance.rationale: This paper addresses, by name, an analytic debt the corpus has explicitly recorded as unformalised. QOU/Archimedean/AwZeroLocalization.lean opens: 'The KSel-2-ID chain's remaining analytic debt (TropicalClassTransport §3, the u1-promotion audit §4 gap 2) is the zero asymptotics of the Ramanujan entire function (q-Airy function) A_w(z) = Sum_{m>=0} w^{m^2}(-z)^m/(w;w)_m', proved in docs/audits/2026-08-01-awzero-asymptotics.md 'by recentring A_w at index n, identifying the limit of the recentred series as a Jacobi theta function whose zero set is the lattice w^{2Z}, and running Rouche against that theta limit', with the note that 'the analytic steps that need complex analysis (Jacobi triple product, Rouche, the argument principle) are NOT formalised here'. Morita's A_q(x) := Sum_{n>=0} q^{n^2}(-x)^n/(q;q)_n (§3.1) is character-for-character the same function, under the same hypothesis 0 < |q| < 1. His main theorem is an EXACT identity writing A_{q^2} as a Jacobi-theta-weighted combination of two q-Airy functions — i.e. a published, exact version of the theta comparison the corpus's audit builds by hand — and his own stated motivation is that 'our new relation shows an asymptotic behavior of the Ramanujan function near the infinity'. Independently corroborating: the corpus's existing ismail2005qairy entry carries the note 'No zero-asymptotics theorem is attributed to it', so the corpus knows it lacks a source for exactly this. The paper also sits inside the q-Borel/q-Laplace framework of Zhang that QOU/MathlibExt/QBorelKernel.lean already builds on.

keyResults.statement: For all x in C*, A_{q^2}(-q^3/x^2) = (1/(q,-1;q)_infinity) * { theta(x/q) Ai_q(-x) + theta(-x/q) Ai_q(x) }, where theta is the Jacobi theta function and Ai_q the q-Painleve q-Airy function.
keyResults.useForFolio: An exact closed-form theta factorisation of the Ramanujan function A_q, valid for all x in C*. The corpus's Rouche argument compares A_w against a theta LIMIT obtained by recentring; this identity is the exact statement that comparison approximates, so the zero asymptotics zeta_n = w^{1-2n}(1 + O(w^n)) can be read off the theta zero lattice with the error controlled by the Ai_q factors rather than by a hand-built limit. Hypotheses check out: 0 < |q| < 1 matches the corpus's 0 < w < 1 (set q^2 = w), and the series definitions coincide exactly.

keyResults.statement: A_q satisfies the q-difference equation (q x sigma_q^2 - sigma_q + 1) u(x) = 0, whose second solution is u(x) = theta(x) * 2phi_0(0,0;-;q,-x) with the 2phi_0 series DIVERGENT.
keyResults.useForFolio: Shows the theta function is intrinsic to the q-difference equation A_q solves — it is the multiplier attached to the divergent second solution, not an artefact of a chosen comparison. That is the structural reason the corpus's theta-limit step works, and it is the level-1 q-Borel kernel picture (t_n = q^{n(n-1)/2}) that QBorelKernel.lean already formalises, now instantiated on a function the corpus actually uses.

keyResults.statement: Jacobi's triple product identity: theta(x) = (q, -x, -q/x; q)_infinity.
keyResults.useForFolio: Exactly one of the three analytic steps AwZeroLocalization.lean names as not formalised ('Jacobi triple product, Rouche, the argument principle'). Having it stated with the paper's own normalisation removes the normalisation ambiguity when that step is eventually formalised or cited.

relevance.rationale: Directly on the corpus's central algebra, but one step to the side of where the compute lives. QOU works with the finite Iwahori-Hecke algebras H_n(q) and their Markov trace; Solleveld works with AFFINE Hecke algebras H(R,q) with possibly unequal parameters. The corpus does have a named affine open item — content/quantum-observable-universe/braids-and-knots/markov-trace-inductive-limit.lean states 'The full operator-theoretic construction (von Neumann inductive limit on the infinite-dim affine Hecke algebra) is the open R&D content' — and Solleveld's Theorem 2 is exactly a structural computation of the homology (hence the trace-functional data) of that algebra, with the striking conclusion that it does not depend on q at all. Held to supporting rather than core because nothing in the current compute path consumes it: QOU's Markov trace is built at finite n from Hoefsmit/Wedderburn data, and the inductive limit is scaffolding, not a live consumer. Honest caveat to carry into any citation: the v3 abstract itself records a 2021 CORRECTION — 'some problems with the construction of families of representations surfaced, these are discussed on pages 16, 18, 19 and 22' — so Theorem 1 must not be cited as unqualified.

keyResults.statement: For epsilon in C outside sqrt(-1)R^*, HH_*(H(R,q^epsilon)) is isomorphic to the W-invariant algebraic differential forms Omega^*(T~)^W on the extended quotient of the torus by the Weyl group — in particular independent of the parameter q.
keyResults.useForFolio: A q-independence statement for the homological invariants of the affine Hecke algebra, which is the structural backdrop for the inductive-limit trace object the corpus leaves open. It says the trace-theoretic data of the algebra is rigid in q, so any q-dependence QOU observes in a Markov-trace-derived quantity must come from the REPRESENTATION/evaluation side, not from the homology of the algebra — a useful, checkable separation of concerns for the fibre-vs-archimedean distinction AGENTS.md insists on.

keyResults.statement: For epsilon outside sqrt(-1)R^*, two representations pi(w,i,t,epsilon) and pi(w',i',t',epsilon) have the SAME TRACE iff w = w', i = i' and t, t' lie in one Z_W(w)-orbit; and the collection forms a Q-basis of the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional H(R,q^epsilon)-representations.
keyResults.useForFolio: A trace-separation criterion: it says precisely which representation data a trace functional can and cannot distinguish. That is the affine analogue of the question QOU's Markov trace answers at finite n (traces separate Wedderburn blocks indexed by partitions), and it is the statement the inductive-limit construction would need in order to know its limiting trace is faithful. Cite with the v3 correction caveat attached.

keyResults.statement: The representations of the family H(R,q^epsilon), epsilon in C, come in families depending analytically on epsilon (matrix coefficients conjecturally algebraic in q^{1/2}).
keyResults.useForFolio: An analyticity-in-the-deformation-parameter statement for Hecke representations. This is the affine instance of the fibre-level framing AGENTS.md sets out for c_k(q) — the object is analytic in q at the fibre level, and each substrate anchor is one evaluation of it. It supports that framing with an external theorem rather than an assertion, though it does not establish it for the finite H_n(q) the corpus computes with.

relevance.rationale: Andersen-Mistegard, resurgence analysis of quantum invariants of Seifert fibered homology spheres. Its Theorem 2 states that the poles of the Borel transform of the Ohtsuki series Z_0(X) coincide with the classical complex Chern-Simons values, and Theorem 3 that the GPPV q-series Z-hat_0(X;q) is a Borel-Laplace resummation of Z_0(X). The corpus applies exactly this principle heuristically: rem:ohtsuki-tower-bar-parity asserts that the Borel-Pade resummation of the odd (Gevrey-1) Ohtsuki sub-tower has its Borel singularity at the real action A = Vol(4_1)/pi, off the imaginary integration ray, hence no Stokes ambiguity -- a statement about where Borel singularities sit relative to complex-CS actions. So the paper supplies the theorem-form of a principle the corpus uses. It is NOT core, and deliberately not aid-proof: the results are proved for Seifert fibered homology spheres, a class the corpus contains no member of, whereas the corpus's object is a hyperbolic knot complement (4_1). Transporting the pole-location theorem across that gap is precisely what would need checking, and this document does not do it.

keyResults.statement: For a Seifert fibered homology sphere X, the poles of the Borel transform of the Ohtsuki series Z_0(X) coincide with the set of classical complex Chern-Simons values CS_C(X).
keyResults.useForFolio: A proved instance of 'Borel singularities sit at complex CS actions', the assumption behind the corpus's placement of the Ohtsuki-tower Borel singularity at Vol(4_1)/pi; usable as corroboration of the principle and as the statement whose hypotheses a knot-complement transfer would have to reproduce.

keyResults.statement: Z-hat_0(X;q) is a Borel-Laplace resummation of the Ohtsuki series Z_0(X), with a full asymptotic expansion as q -> exp(2 pi i / k) recovering the WRT invariant tau_k(X).
keyResults.useForFolio: The resummation-side template for the corpus's open multi-instanton / median-resummation residual on the one-instanton normalization (the quantitatively open leg of the u(q_0) map).

The corpus's Borel-Pade probe locates a singularity at A = Vol(4_1)/pi ~ 0.646; Thm 2 says (in its own class) such singularities are exactly complex-CS actions. Cross-checking the probe's numerically located singularity against the 4_1 complex-CS spectrum is a cross-check to run, not a number to adopt.

relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan, and the folio has three blocks whose whole purpose is comparison with standard nuclear physics: rem:bw-mass-decomposition-dictionary (states the goal of replacing the empirical Bethe-Weizsaecker equation with substrate-only input, and that the absolute per-isotope binding closure is open), rem:feynman-qou-comparison (contrasts the five fitted SEMF coefficients with the zero-fitted-parameter Wedderburn formula, and says the Wedderburn error tracks the shell model), and rem:q-deformed-nuclear-models-comparison (compares against q-deformed oscillator models). All three compare against 1930s-1950s phenomenology. None cites the modern effective-field-theory framework, which is the actual state of the art and the thing a referee will ask about. This document is the authoritative review of the three main nuclear EFTs (Chiral, Pionless, Halo/Cluster), their scales, ranges of applicability and the ab initio few- and many-body results built on them. It supplies no theorem the folio derives from, so it is supporting, not core — but the omission is a real weakness in a comparison section. I read the abstract, author block and table of contents opening; I did not read the body chapters, and I am not claiming any specific numerical benchmark from it.

keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the comparison blocks a modern benchmark rather than only the semi-empirical mass formula and the shell model, and states the applicability ranges against which the folio's light-nuclei-only reach should be positioned.

relevance.rationale: No text layer (Xerox scan; pdftotext, pypdf and pdfminer all return 0 chars), so read as rendered page images. It constructs a hierarchy of linking integrals whose second-order member is the Gauss/helicity integral and whose third-order member (a Massey-product integral) detects the Borromean rings, with a fourth-order member distinguishing a 4-component Brunnian entanglement from four unlinked rings, and it recasts the whole hierarchy for BRAIDS as a hierarchy of winding numbers. That last move is the reason this is core rather than supporting. The corpus's EM-linking front (bean qou-o6ml, docs/audits/2026-08-01-em-linking-reads-round1.md) is stuck on two obstructions established from the existing helicity cluster (dgkmsv, komendarczyk, khesin, cantarella-deturck-gluck): total antisymmetry of mu-bar(123), and the absence of any per-pair splitting of the Theorem-B integrand. Separately, MilnorIndeterminacyGate.lean proves that a Hopf-linked spectator collapses the mu-bar residue space to ZMod 1, i.e. the LINK invariant carries no triple content in the mixed-bond regime — which is the regime the mixed-multibond probe operates in. The third-order winding number here (eq. 22, Psi_ijk = Re integral of lambda_ij d lambda_jk + cyclic, built from the Arnol'd generators omega_ij of the braid-group cohomology) is stated as a well-defined BRAID invariant 'irrespective of whether the net second order winding numbers vanish'. The corpus's substrate is braid words in B_n, so a braid-level third-order invariant that survives nonzero pairwise winding is directly constructible here and is a different object from every invariant the EM-linking sweep has already excluded. None of this is in references.ts (no entry for this work or for the third-order-winding-number construction it cites).

keyResults.statement: The one-form psi_ijk = lambda_ij d lambda_jk + lambda_jk d lambda_ki + lambda_ki d lambda_ij is closed by the Arnol'd relation, so Psi_ijk = Re integral over gamma of psi_ijk is a homotopy-invariant third-order winding number of a 3-string braid, well defined whether or not the net second-order winding numbers vanish.
keyResults.useForFolio: A braid-level third-order invariant that is NOT killed by a Hopf-linked spectator, unlike the mu-bar residue that MilnorIndeterminacyGate.lean collapses to ZMod 1. relevance.rationale: A 2018 Sorbonne doctoral thesis on Reidemeister torsion over character varieties: chapter 2 develops the ADJOINT torsion as a differential form on the character variety, with Main Theorem 1 describing its behaviour at a finite point (and interpreting the singularities via the Alexander polynomial); chapter 3 treats the standard torsion function and both torsions at ideal points. The corpus uses adjoint Reidemeister torsion at one point only -- the discrete faithful structure -- via the Dimofte-Garoufalidis 1-loop invariant |det J_NZ| (borromean_nz_adjoint_torsion.py, whitehead_c_sigma_torsion.py, and the 2026-08-02 unified cusp law exp(2 c_0) = 2^{c-1} / |det J_NZ|). Treating the torsion as a function on the whole character variety, with controlled poles and normalization at ideal points, is the natural technique for the one honest open sub-item that audit records: the general-c derivation of the per-cusp factor 2^{(c-1)/2}, currently pinned only on c = 1, 2, 3. That is a normalization question and this thesis is about torsion normalization -- but whether its conventions actually produce that factor is unverified, so this is new-remark, not aid-proof.

keyResults.statement: The adjoint Reidemeister torsion is realized as a form on the character variety whose behaviour at finite points is controlled (singularities interpreted through the Alexander polynomial), with a separate analysis at ideal points.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the variety-level normalization framework in which the corpus's empirically-pinned per-cusp factor 2^{(c-1)/2} in the 1-loop cusp law would have to be derived or refuted.

relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan; a doctoral thesis on Laplacian eigenvalue multiplicities of constant-negative-curvature surfaces with large symmetry groups, treating the Bolza surface (genus 2, automorphism group GL_2(Z_3) semidirect Z_2) and the Klein quartic (genus 3, PGL_2(Z_7) semidirect Z_2), proving mult(lambda_1) = 3 and mult(lambda_2) = 4 for Bolza and mult(lambda_1) in {6,7,8} for the Klein quartic, with numerical eigenvalue appendices for those surfaces and the Fermat quartic. The folio's central object is a genus-4 surface with automorphism group S_5 — the exact next member of that family — and content/quantum-observable-universe/brings-surface/hyperelliptic-quintic.md already places a folio surface 'in the Bolza family' citing bolza1887. So the METHOD (decompose L^2 of the surface into irreducibles of the automorphism group, then bound eigenvalue multiplicities representation-theoretically) transfers directly. Honest limits: the thesis does NOT treat the genus-4 case, the Bolza lambda_1 result is stated as conditional on a further conjecture with numerical evidence, and — the reason this is not core — grep finds no folio claim about a Laplacian spectral gap or first eigenvalue on its surface for the method to serve. It is a technique source with no current consumer.

keyResults.statement: Representation-theoretic decomposition under the full automorphism group determines Laplacian eigenvalue multiplicities on maximally symmetric hyperbolic surfaces: multiplicity 3 for lambda_1 and 4 for lambda_2 on the Bolza surface (the lambda_1 result conditional on a stated conjecture supported numerically).
keyResults.useForFolio: The transferable method for any future folio claim about the Laplacian spectrum of its genus-4 S_5-symmetric surface; the numerical appendices give reference eigenvalues for the neighbouring genus-2 and genus-3 cases.

The two .md citations also check out: mass-endomorphism/channel-rotation-askey-lit.md:30 claims the state integral factors into a q-series and a q-tilde series with leading asymptotics tracing Vol + i*CS, and the source supports both halves (restrictions to C minus R factorize bilinearly as finite sums of products of a q-series and a q-tilde series; the leading asymptotic exponent of the new matrices involves the complex volume); mass-endomorphism/complex-volume-character-variety-path.md:19 uses it only as consistency framing, which is within scope. relevance.rationale: A 10-page note whose headline theorem (infinitely many non-hyperelliptic genus-3 surfaces with Aut acting transitively on the Weierstrass points) is not something the folio consumes. Its *second* theorem is: for g > 2 with simple Weierstrass points, a transitive action occurs iff g = 4 and X is Bring's curve, or g = 3 and X is one of the C_t (t != 0,3). That is a sharp, citable uniqueness characterisation of Bring's curve, and ex:chi-minus-six-derivation Step 7 currently asserts 'the unique maximally symmetric genus-4 curve is Bring's surface' with no source. Reading it also surfaces a discrepancy worth the author's attention (below): the same block's Step 5 speaks of 'the 6 Weierstrass points of Bring's surface', whereas transitivity plus simplicity forces a single Aut-orbit of g^3-g = 60 weight-1 points -- and the corpus already records exactly that count from Braden-Disney-Hogg in docs/audits/2026-07-18-uploaded-papers-binding-mass-gap-ideas.md line 409 ('60 weight-1 Weierstrass points, Aut-transitive'). Per the corpus-grep discipline this is flagged as an internal inconsistency between a content block and an existing audit, not as a new discovery, and not as a claim that chi(A) = -6 is wrong: the '6 branch points' conclusion may well be right for another reason, but the parenthetical derivation 'from the S_3 subset S_5 orbits on the 6 Weierstrass points' cannot be read as stated if there are 60 of them in one orbit.

keyResults.statement: For g > 2 with simple Weierstrass points, Aut(X) acts transitively on the Weierstrass points iff g = 4 and X is Bring's curve, or g = 3 and X is C_t for some t != 0, 3; and Bring's curve is listed with Klein's quartic and Macbeath's curve among the classically known transitive examples.

So the paper is the canonical citable source for the language the keystone is phrased in. relevance.rationale: Mironov-Morozov on a 'combinatorial Borel transform': averaging Cauchy identities for Schur functions over the power-sum variables p_k, which rescales the combinatorial factors (d_R and the like) in sums over Young diagrams the way the ordinary exponential Borel transform rescales factorials, thereby unifying a collection of previously scattered single-Schur-sum identities and their skew-Schur counterparts. Two superficially matching corpus vocabularies do not in fact match. (i) The corpus's Borel front is resurgent -- the Borel transform of an asymptotic series in hbar = log q, its plane singularities and Stokes structure -- not a reweighting of diagram sums. (ii) The corpus's Young-diagram object is the fixed-n Frobenius pairing tr_M = sum_{lambda |- n} y_lambda chi^lambda over the Wedderburn blocks of H_n(q), and Delta_lambda = (-1)^{n(lambda)} dim V_lambda; the identities here are generating sums over ALL diagrams, with no fixed-n truncation and no q-deformation of the Hecke kind. I could not name a corpus place that wants one of these identities, so per the skill the key-results list is empty. Scope-(a): as read, nothing usable; averaged-Schur techniques are not thereby excluded from the covariance-kernel front.

relevance.rationale: rem:st-is-median-resummation identifies the surreal standard part st with the Ecalle median resummation L^med and leans on 'the unique real single-valued average' being well defined; conj:kashaev-surreal applies exactly that to the Kashaev transseries at a root of unity. Both currently cite only ecalle1981 and berarducci-mantova2018 -- i.e. the general theory -- while in quantum topology the existence and radial-limit behaviour of S^med is Conjecture 1.1 of Costin-Garoufalidis, still open in general. This paper proves Conjecture 1.1 parts (1) and (2), plus an explicit radial-limit formula (part 3), for every Habiro-ring element Phi_f admitting a strange identity to a partial theta series with even, mean-zero periodic f (Thm 1.2), and derives the full conjecture for the torus-knot families T(2,2u+1) and T(3,2k) (Cor 1.5). That converts the folio's 'conjecturally well-defined median resummation' into 'proved on a named class', which is precisely the epistemic status rem:st-is-median-resummation should be recording. Explicit scope caveat, and the reason no aid-proof is proposed: the hypothesis is a strange identity to a partial theta series, which the trefoil/torus-knot Kontsevich-Zagier series satisfy and the *hyperbolic* 4_1 tail S(q) = sum prod (1-q^j)(1-q^{-j}) of prop:habiro-tail-archimedean-action does NOT. Citing this at the 4_1 block must therefore be a scope statement ('proved for the torus families, open for 4_1'), never a discharge.

relevance.rationale: The corpus opened a live derivation route on 2026-08-07 (docs/audits/2026-08-07-extended-bloch-group-fixes-the-normalization-fit.md, beans qou-78pt / qou-l2t2) whose central claim is verbatim 'Neumann's extended Bloch group is the canonical resolution of exactly that ambiguity' — the branch-of-logarithm ambiguity that made the Markov-normalization route a fit. This document's §3 is exactly that missing statement: I read pp.7-9 and it gives the Bloch group B(F) as ker(d: Z[F] -> Lambda^2 F^x) modulo the 5-term relation, the extended Bloch group with the lifted 5-term relation on pairs (u,v) with e^u = 1 - e^v, and the extended regulator into C/4pi^2 Z whose imaginary and real parts are volume and Chern-Simons. §4 additionally gives the half-symplectic completion of the Neumann-Zagier matrix H = (A B), which is the structure behind the det J_NZ(B_3) object the corpus's 1-loop witness uses. Honest scope caveat: this is a SURVEY, so it is an authoritative statement plus a pointer, not the original theorem; the primary sources for the extended Bloch group are cited inside it as its [30] (Neumann) and [21,39] (Zickert, Goette) and those should be registered too if the route matures. I am rating it core because the corpus demonstrably should be citing an extended-Bloch-group source right now and cites none.

relevance.rationale: Introduces topological volume volt(M), the smallest volume of the complement of a (possibly empty) hyperbolic link in a closed 3-manifold M, and computes it for families of non-hyperbolic manifolds. Two of its statements bear directly on assertions the corpus makes without a source. (1) The corpus repeatedly justifies its choice of the figure-eight knot as 'the simplest hyperbolic knot', described in one audit as making Vol(4_1)/hbar_q^2 carry 'no free parameter', and in three-calibration-inputs-proof as 'simplest hyperbolic knot invariant' -- always as an informal appeal, never with a citation. Example 2.1 of this document states volt(S^3) = 2 v_0 = 2.02988 with the figure-eight knot as the minimiser, i.e. the figure-eight complement is the MINIMAL-volume hyperbolic link complement in the three-sphere. That converts an unsourced hand-wave into a precise minimality theorem, and the numerical value 2 v_0 (twice the ideal regular tetrahedron) matches the corpus's Vol(4_1) = 2*Cl_2(pi/3) exactly, so no external number is being adopted -- the corpus's own value is being characterised. (2) The Borromean rings are listed among the known universal links, meaning every closed orientable 3-manifold is a branched cover of the three-sphere over them, with Cor. 2.11 giving volt(M) <= d_L(M) volH(L). A framework whose nucleon IS the Borromean link should know that its nucleon knot is universal in that sense; the corpus has no occurrence of 'universal link' in this sense anywhere. Corpus-grep run over docs/audits/, docs/coordination/, content/ and computations/ for 'universal link', 'minimal volume', 'smallest volume' and the Cao--Meyerhoff minimality: no prior closure found.

keyResults.statement: volt(S^3) = 2 v_0 ~ 2.02988, where v_0 is the volume of the ideal regular tetrahedron, with the figure-eight knot complement realising the minimum among hyperbolic link complements in the three-sphere.

relevance.rationale: Studies a real-valued invariant of closed 3-manifolds defined as the smallest volume of the complement of a (possibly empty) hyperbolic link in the manifold: basic properties, asymptotically tight upper and lower bounds, a classification of all non-hyperbolic closed 3-manifolds with the invariant at most 3.07, and the determination of the minimising link in lens spaces via Dehn filling. Its relevance here is as the literature answer to a standing exposure in the corpus: several blocks assign hyperbolic volume 0 to every torus knot and read that vanishing as physics ('torus knots carry zero hyperbolic volume, representing the massless, force-carrying sector'; Vol(3_1) = Vol(5_1) = Vol(Hopf) = 0 in building-block-knots.lean). Zero is correct for the Gromov-norm volume of a Seifert-fibred complement, but it is a property of the chosen invariant, and this document is the construction that gives every 3-manifold a unified, generally nonzero volume by minimising over hyperbolic links. That is exactly the objection a referee raises at the massless-sector claim, made precise. It is NOT load-bearing: the invariant is defined for closed manifolds, so it does not directly redefine the corpus's Vol(K) for a knot complement in S^3, and no corpus derivation changes.

keyResults.useForFolio: Lets the corpus state honestly that Vol = 0 on torus knots is a statement about the hyperbolic-volume invariant, not the absence of any volume, and cite the alternative rather than leaving the claim exposed.

keyResults.statement: The triton and helium-4 binding energies are not independent: two-body interactions constrain them to a correlation band, and an irreducible three-nucleon force is required to fix the triton, after which helium-4 is reproduced.

relevance.rationale: Scanned journal article with no usable text layer (pdftotext returns only the download banner for all 17 pages); identified by rendering page 1 as an image and reading it directly. It formulates the electroweak theory over the QUATERNIONS: fermions and Higgs mesons are defined over H, the unit quaternions realise the gauge SU(2), and the construction reproduces the left-right symmetric SU(2)_L x SU(2)_R x U(1) theory at the phenomenological level while offering an algebraic explanation for the replication of quarks and leptons in flavour doublets. The corpus contains QOU/QuaternionicElectroweak.lean, whose docstring and declarations implement that construction essentially verbatim -- a fermion doublet is one quaternion (its four real degrees of freedom being the two complex degrees of a standard SU(2) doublet), IsSU2 is the unit-norm condition, su2L is left multiplication, su2R is right multiplication, and u1Y_isSU2 places the hypercharge phase inside SU(2) -- with no citation of any kind. That is a provenance gap: a library Lean file independently re-deriving a published 1982 construction. It is also a constraint, not just an attribution: bring_tetraplectic.md is explicit that identifying its Reeb-triad SU(2) with a physical gauge symmetry is 'interpretive, not derived', and this document's analysis says the natural gauge group of the quaternionic construction is LEFT-RIGHT SYMMETRIC, which the Standard Model is not at accessible energies. So the prior art both supplies the missing attribution and sharpens the open question the corpus has already flagged as interpretive.

keyResults.statement: Formulating fermions and Higgs mesons over the quaternions reproduces the left-right symmetric SU(2)_L x SU(2)_R x U(1) electroweak theory phenomenologically, gives an algebraic account of the replication of quarks and leptons in flavour doublets, and correlates the breakdown to U(1)_em with the existence of a Fock space for gauge singlets but not for quaternionic states.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the missing attribution for the corpus's quaternionic-electroweak Lean file and, more usefully, tells the corpus what its own construction predicts: a left-right symmetric gauge group, which is a testable consequence of the interpretive identification bring_tetraplectic.md already flags as underived.

relevance.rationale: NOT AN ORPHAN -- the slice was seeded as orphan and that is wrong. The paper's sectioning is 1.1-1.6 then 2.1 'Dilogarithm and partitions', 2.2 characters of affine Kac--Moody algebras, 2.3 dilogarithm identities and algebraic K-theory, 2.4 connection with crystal basis, 2.5 quantum dilogarithm; its numbered results are Propositions A-H plus Proposition 1 and Proposition 2. Separately, the Lean file's definition of the truncated symmetric q-dilogarithm sum z^n/(n [n]_q) carries '-- Ref: [kirillov1995] Sec. 2.1', but Sec. 2.1 is about partitions; the q-dilogarithm is Definition 9 in Sec. 2.5, and it is the ASYMMETRIC form sum x^n/(n(1-q^n)), a different normalisation from the corpus's symmetric [n]_q version. Corpus-grep over docs/audits/, content/, computations/, docs/coordination/: no Higgs-bundle or spectral-curve treatment exists anywhere in the tree, so this is a genuine absence rather than a duplicate.

The corpus is full of q-difference structures -- the Habiro c_k recursion, the AJ/q-holonomic machinery, the q-Bessel kernel -- and already registers a reference on the local analytic classification and q-Stokes phenomena, but the Tate curve C*/q^Z appears NOWHERE in the corpus (grep over content/ and docs/audits/ returns zero). Two honest limits keep it supporting rather than core: the theory is stated for |q| < 1 while the substrate q_0 ~ 1.10998 exceeds 1 (the bar involution maps it into range, but that step must be made explicitly, not assumed), and no corpus claim is currently wrong or unsourced for want of this. relevance.rationale: The 1913 Proc. Amer. Acad. paper that poses and solves the generalized Riemann problem -- characterizing a function by monodromy-type constants independent of its defining equation -- for linear differential equations and, in the allied cases, for linear DIFFERENCE and q-DIFFERENCE equations. This is the origin of the Birkhoff connection matrix, and the corpus is standing on it: QOU/QBeta/BirkhoffAmplitudeWellPosed.lean and BirkhoffAmplitudeE.lean pin the A=3 anti-self-adjoint amplitude E to the GLOBAL 0-to-infinity Birkhoff connection matrix P = (X^infty)^{-1} X^0 of the C1 carrier, and the q-Borel attack plan's stage S3 names the 'Birkhoff-Guenther normal-form extraction' and the 'q-analog of Birkhoff-Malgrange-Sibuya'. All of these cite only the modern RSZ Asterisque; the primary source is unregistered. Explicitly NOT aid-proof: Birkhoff's q-difference theory is the REGULAR (connection-matrix) setting, and the corpus's live obstruction, per the 2026-08-08 closure audit, is an IRREGULAR pure-isoclinic point (slope 1/2, k = 1) where no connection-matrix classification applies. It grounds the vocabulary and the global object; it does not supply the missing Stokes data.

keyResults.locator: the q-difference sections of the 1913 memoir (the 'allied problems')
keyResults.statement: For a linear q-difference system, the analytic solution is characterized by connection constants relating canonical solutions at 0 and at infinity -- the Birkhoff connection matrix -- and the associated Riemann problem asks for those constants to be prescribed at will.
keyResults.useForFolio: The primary source for the global object BirkhoffAmplitudeWellPosed.lean reasons about (P = (X^infty)^{-1} X^0 and the gauge freedom of the canonical local solutions), which currently cites only the modern RSZ treatment.

relevance.rationale: Shows the set of cusp shapes of hyperbolic tunnel-number-one manifolds is dense in the Teichmuller space of the torus (Thm 1.1), with the analogue for tunnel number n (Thm 1.2), and consequences for exceptional Dehn fillings. Its value here is definitional rather than theorem-level: the corpus uses 'cusp shape' load-bearingly and without any source. prop:cusp-shape-bar-parity asserts the cusp shape of the figure-eight is a primitive sixth root of unity and splits it under the bar-involution; rem:winding-lattice-norm-form then builds a cusp lattice Z<1, omega> on that value, and rem:meridian-holonomy-boost hangs the meridian holonomy off it. Under the standard definition used here -- the similarity class of the Euclidean torus induced on the cusp cross-section, a point of Teichmuller space -- e^{i pi/3} is the shape of the equilateral triangles tiling that cross-section (the ideal regular tetrahedron parameter), which is not obviously the same object as the meridian-longitude modulus of the cusp torus. That is a discrepancy worth resolving before more weight is put on the cusp lattice, and it is why the proposed action is a remark pinning the definition, not a citation asserting agreement.

keyResults.locator: sec. 3 ("Recall that the Teichmuller space of the torus is the space of similarity classes...") + Def. 2.1-2.4
keyResults.statement: The cusp shape of a hyperbolic 3-manifold with torus boundary is the similarity class of the Euclidean structure induced on a neighbourhood of that boundary, i.e. a point of the Teichmuller space of the torus.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the standard definition for a term the corpus uses in at least three blocks with no source, and against which its value for the figure-eight should be checked.

keyResults.statement: Cusp shapes of hyperbolic tunnel-number-one manifolds are dense in the Teichmuller space of the torus.
keyResults.useForFolio: Background only: it says the cusp shape is not constrained by low tunnel number, so no structural conclusion can be drawn from a particular knot's cusp shape being special.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry, and no source anywhere in the corpus for the notion of cusp shape despite three blocks depending on it.

relevance.rationale: Studies incomplete hyperbolic structures on the figure-eight knot complement. The deformations are parametrised by an open subset of a plane affine curve C of degree four with two ordinary double points, hence of genus one; the paper gives an explicit birational map from C to a nonsingular Weierstrass cubic E defined over Q, and exhibits a concrete correspondence between the closed 3-manifolds arising from degenerations (Sol-manifolds, Haken manifolds decomposing along an embedded torus, Euclidean orbifolds) and points of finite order on E, with the Haken cases corresponding exactly to the rational points, which form a cyclic group of order four. This is a genuinely arithmetic structure on the deformation space of the corpus's single most-used hyperbolic knot -- the figure-eight is the Higgs entry in the fundamental-knots table and the muon anchor Vol(4_1)/hbar_q^2 in the mass formula. Blocks such as prop:cusp-shape-bar-parity and prop:figure-eight-reeb-rotation work with that complement's cusp and deformation data with no arithmetic classification available to them. It is supporting, not core: no corpus claim depends on the degeneration classification today, and the corpus's own elliptic curve (the Descartes curve) is a different object, so the connection must be established rather than assumed. Its likely value is as a prune -- an enumeration of what the figure-eight deformation space can degenerate to, bounded by a torsion group of order four, is the kind of finite structural constraint that narrows a search before it is run.

keyResults.locator: Sec. 1 (Introduction), with the curve C at (1)-(2) and the Weierstrass model E at (4)
keyResults.statement: The deformation curve of incomplete hyperbolic structures on the figure-eight knot complement has genus one and is birational to an elliptic curve E over Q; degenerations correspond to points of finite order on E, and the Haken cases correspond exactly to the rational points of E, a cyclic group of order four.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies a finite arithmetic classification of what the corpus's muon-anchor knot complement can degenerate to, which bounds any attempt to deform that anchor and gives the cusp/Reeb blocks an arithmetic handle they currently lack.

proposedActions.rationale: The figure-eight complement is the corpus's most-used hyperbolic object and its deformation space has an explicit arithmetic classification that the corpus does not cite anywhere.

relevance.rationale: Constructs concrete genus-g hyperbolic surfaces that arise as totally geodesic boundary components of compact orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds, by taking a hyperbolic 3-manifold with one torus cusp and connected totally geodesic boundary and performing hyperbolic Dehn surgery on the toral end, then distinguishing the results via lengths of short geodesics and their positions in Teichmueller/moduli space. The hyperbolic-3-manifold and Dehn-surgery setting overlaps the corpus's, and there is a superficially attractive hook — the folio's state space is a genus-4 object (Bring's surface; knots embed in a 'genus-4 handlebody'). But the hook does not close: grep finds zero occurrences of 'totally geodesic' anywhere in content/, computations/ or docs/; the corpus's genus-4 handlebody is used topologically as an embedding constraint, never asserted to carry a hyperbolic structure with totally geodesic boundary; and Bring's surface enters as an algebraic curve with S_5 automorphisms forced by chi = -6, not as a point of moduli space selected by geodesic lengths. So there is no named place that wants this result. Scope-(a): this document, as read, supplies nothing usable here.

proposedActions.rationale: Read and judged to need nothing. If the folio ever asserts a hyperbolic structure on the genus-4 boundary (rather than a topological handlebody), this becomes relevant; today it does not.

relevance.rationale: A 30-page French survey of q-difference equations by the four authors whose Asterisque memoir the corpus's whole C1-at-infinity front is built on. Sections: 2 (q-difference modules, gauge transformation, meromorphic continuation), 3 (local and global classification, confluence of the connection matrix, 3.5 local classification of IRREGULAR equations), 4 (summability of formal solutions, 4.3 q-analogue Borel-Laplace summations), 5 (arithmetic q-difference equations). Two things make it core rather than background. First, the 2026-08-08 closure audit ended by ruling that the surviving route must be 'q-native' -- and section 4 is precisely the q-native summation toolbox, independent of the slope-filtration apparatus that closed. Second, and specifically: section 4.4 is titled 'the series (sum_n q^{n(n-1)/2} x^n)^2 is not summable at a single level', with Remark 4.12 computing that its q-Borel transform is meromorphic with simple poles in q^N and q-exponential growth of order EXACTLY TWO at infinity. The corpus's level-1 kernel is literally t_n = q^{C(n,2)} = q^{n(n-1)/2} (QOU/MathlibExt/QBorelKernel.lean), and its own budget table records that after dividing the proved deg_q(c_n) = n^2 by that kernel a residual of order n^2/2 survives at every level d, i.e. 'no level d absorbs the n^2 growth'. That is the same failure mode, worked as a published counterexample, and it names a resolution direction (multiple levels) alongside the ramification reading the corpus's stage S1 adopted. The corpus's own S1 note flags that its answer is 'a degree-budget determination, not a theorem about RSZ's analytic construction', so a second published reading of the same obstruction is directly wanted.

keyResults.statement: The square of the level-1 series sum_n q^{n(n-1)/2} x^n is not q-Borel-Laplace summable at a single level, even though the series itself is; its q-Borel transform B_{q;1} is meromorphic with simple poles in q^N and q-exponential growth of order exactly two at infinity.
keyResults.useForFolio: A published instance of the corpus's own degree-budget negative ('no level d absorbs the n^2 growth') against exactly the corpus's kernel q^{C(n,2)}, giving a multi-level alternative to the ramification reading stage S1 adopted, and a template for the residual-order bookkeeping.

keyResults.statement: The q-analogue Borel-Laplace summation: q-Borel transform, summation along a direction, and the resulting Stokes multiplier interpretation.
keyResults.useForFolio: The q-native summation machinery the closure audit says the work must move to, stated by the same authors and independent of the slope-filtration classification that closed.

proposedActions.rationale: The survey by the RSZ authors covering exactly the q-native summation front the corpus is moving to, with no bibliography entry.

Re-run the attack plan's degree-budget table against the Sec. 4.4 example: compare the corpus's residual (deg c_n = n^2 against t_n = q^{C(n,2)}) with the 'order exactly two' q-Borel growth Rmk 4.12 computes, and record whether the C1 series is, up to gauge, of the multi-level type that example exhibits. This is a comparison to run, not a result to adopt.

Deliberately not aid-proof. Sec. 4.4 is an example about a specific series, not a theorem about C1; whether C1's infinity-side formal solution falls in that class is exactly the open stage-S1 question, and the corpus's ramified level-2 answer is an alternative reading, not a contradiction. Record both readings and what would discriminate them.

relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan, and after a careful read of the abstract, index terms and introduction the honest verdict is no bearing. This is statistical signal processing / kernel learning. The word 'quaternion' does appear in 16 folio content files, which is exactly the kind of lexical coincidence that inflates a triage: those hits are the SU(2)-to-SO(3) double cover (rem:quaternion-so3-motivation, su2-so3-intro) and quaternionic spectral resolvents on the folio's surface — quaternions as a geometric structure, not as a scalar field over which one builds an RKHS for regression. There is no kernel method, no learning problem and no regression anywhere in the folio. Recording this as not-relevant rather than tangential because the field itself does not overlap; the shared word does.

relevance.rationale: Part II of a programme constructing Weyl-group representations on the homology of the conormal variety via invariant eigendistributions and characteristic cycles, covering Springer theory (sec. 4), coherent families, harmonic polynomials, nilpotent orbital integrals, and an appendix proving the construction agrees with the Kazhdan-Lusztig one. The corpus's alg:delta-lambda-closure names its per-partition weight 'the signed Springer dimension' -- Delta_lambda = (-1)^{n(lambda)} dim V_lambda -- with no citation to the Springer literature anywhere in the tree ('Springer' appears in content/ only in that phrase and in publisher names). The same intersection carries the PROBE-4 prune, which turns on Kazhdan-Lusztig non-negativity being unable to supply a mixed-sign target. This paper is a geometric construction of exactly those two objects and of their comparison. Supporting, not core: the corpus's Delta_lambda value is already Lean-proved sorry-free, so nothing here aids a proof, and this is one construction of the Springer correspondence rather than the canonical primary for the degree/b-invariant statement the corpus's sign convention leans on.

keyResults.statement: Weyl-group representations are constructed on the (Borel-Moore) homology of the conormal variety via an integral formula for invariant eigendistributions, yielding the Springer representations.
keyResults.useForFolio: The geometric backdrop for the phrase 'signed Springer dimension' that alg:delta-lambda-closure uses without a source.

keyResults.statement: The homotopy action constructed here agrees with the Kazhdan-Lusztig construction of the Weyl-group action on the conormal variety.
keyResults.useForFolio: Relevant to the PROBE-4 prune's framing, which contrasts the mixed-sign Delta_lambda target against the non-negativity of Kazhdan-Lusztig multiplicities; the comparison shows the two constructions of the same W-action are not independent sources of a sign.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry, and no Springer-theory citation exists anywhere in the corpus despite the Delta_lambda value being described as a signed Springer dimension.

relevance.rationale: Derives an explicit formula for the colored Jones polynomial J_K(n) of the 2-bridge knot S(p,t), with a more explicit form for twist knots, and deduces a relation between the degree of the colored Jones polynomial and the crossing number for two specific 2-bridge families. This matters here because the corpus's deuteron closure is 6_2, which its own bibliography note identifies as two-bridge with fraction 11/3, and the 5_2 knot used in the one-loop cross-check probe is likewise two-bridge. The corpus currently depends on the two-bridge property only through a cited literature theorem about the one-loop invariant and adjoint torsion; it has no direct colored-Jones computation for these knots at all -- a grep for 'two-bridge'/'2-bridge' across computations/ returns nothing. An explicit closed formula for J_{S(p,t)}(n) would let the corpus compute rather than cite for exactly the knots its deuteron argument rests on. Supporting rather than core: the corpus's existing claims are literature-backed and not in doubt, so this converts an assumption into a check rather than fixing an error. The degree-versus-crossing-number corollary is stated for two specific families and I have not verified that 6_2 lies in either, so no claim is made about it here.

keyResults.locator: Sec. 1 and the main formula for J_{S(p,t)}(n)
keyResults.statement: An explicit formula is given for the colored Jones polynomial of the 2-bridge knot S(p,t) in Schubert notation, specialising to a more explicit form for twist knots.
keyResults.useForFolio: Enables a direct colored-Jones computation for 5_2 and 6_2 -- the corpus's one-loop cross-check knot and its deuteron closure -- where the corpus currently has only a literature dependency and no compute.

proposedActions.rationale: The corpus leans on the two-bridge property of 6_2 for a literature-backed torsion result but registers no reference giving the colored Jones of two-bridge knots explicitly.

relevance.rationale: A survey of the motivic fundamental group of the projective line minus three points and its relation to multiple zeta values: Belyi's theorem and the faithful Galois action on the profinite fundamental group, the pro-unipotent completion and its mixed-Tate-motive structures, motivic periods, and the motivic Galois group acting on them. The corpus makes exactly these moves in prose with no citations at all: rem:transcendental-accounting asserts that the depth-3 Bring periods Li_3(zeta_5^k) span a 4-dimensional Q-vector space on which S_5 acts irreducibly and that 'their post-archimedean structure is governed by the motivic Galois group, not by the q-rational pre-image', and rem:vol-as-motivic-period asserts each Bloch-Wigner value D(z_i) is a Kontsevich-Zagier period — both blocks contain zero \cite. There is also a registered q-deformed multiple-polylogarithm reference whose own scope note warns that it supplies no q-analogue of the {0,1,infinity} picture and points at an open bean; this survey is the classical side of exactly that picture. Supporting rather than core: it is a review, it supplies the framework and vocabulary the corpus's period claims presuppose, but no single theorem here is consumed by a derivation.

keyResults.statement: The pro-unipotent completion of the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} carries the structures of a mixed Tate motive over Z, and its periods are the multiple zeta values, on which the motivic Galois group acts.
keyResults.useForFolio: The citable framework for rem:transcendental-accounting's 'governed by the motivic Galois group' claim and rem:vol-as-motivic-period's Kontsevich-Zagier period claim, both currently uncited.

relevance.rationale: A 2025 Boise State MSc thesis giving a careful exposition of the Andersen-Garoufalidis-Kashaev state-integral over an archimedean local field: the construction from an ideal triangulation with balanced angle data valued in a Gaussian group, convergence of the integrand as a tempered distribution under positivity and a homological constraint, the pentagon identity for the angle-deformed quantum dilogarithm Psi_{a,c} supporting 2-3 Pachner invariance, and gauge invariance under changes of internal angle data. It contributes no new theorem -- it re-derives results the corpus's primary sources already own -- so its key-results list is empty per the skill's rule. It is nonetheless worth registering as a readable secondary account of two objects the corpus asserts: the operator pentagon Phi(P)Phi(Q) = Phi(Q)Phi(P+Q)Phi(P) in rem:q-dilogarithm-pentagon-associator, and the balanced-angle-structure setting the corpus's angle-structure LP/SDP dictionary uses. Reading it surfaced a separate citation gap worth recording (see the actions).

relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan. It establishes a bijection between states on the part arc-graph of a link projection (from the universal R-matrix of U_q(sl(2,C))) and states on the bichromatic digraph of the Garoufalidis-Loebl state sum, giving a new elementary proof of the knot state-sum formula, extending it from knots to links, and — the part that gives it a target here — discussing in detail the computation of the arc-graph state-sum for 3-BRAID CLOSURES. The folio's two canonical objects are exactly 3-braid closures: fundamental-knots-operator-basis records 4_1 = (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1})^2 and the Borromean rings L6a4 = (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1})^3. So this supplies a genuinely independent combinatorial route to the same colored Jones data the folio obtains from the Hecke Markov trace, on precisely the braids the folio uses. That is a cross-check opportunity, not a result the folio consumes, hence supporting. Note the paper is a reconciliation result: its own conclusion is that the two state models are 'in fact not essentially distinct', so it should not be cited as offering a genuinely new invariant.

keyResults.statement: The R-matrix state sum on the part arc-graph and the Garoufalidis-Loebl bichromatic-digraph state sum are related by an explicit bijection of state sets, the formula extends from knots to links, and the arc-graph state-sum is computed explicitly for 3-braid closures.
keyResults.useForFolio: An independent state-sum route to the colored Jones polynomial of the folio's own canonical 3-braid closures, usable to cross-check the Markov-trace computation of tr_M on those words.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; supplies an independent computation route for the exact 3-braid closures the folio's operator basis is built from.

relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan; a doctoral thesis (123 pp.) on the motivic Galois action on motivic fundamental groups of punctured elliptic and rational curves, written in the motivic-correlator programme. Its Chapter 2 is 'Shuffle relations for Hodge and motivic correlators on P^1' — double shuffle relations on correlators — and §1.2.3 treats multiple polylogarithms; Chapter 3 relates Bianchi hyperbolic threefolds and modular complexes to the Galois Lie coalgebra, with §3.4.2 degenerating to Voronoi complexes and multiple zeta values. The folio has a specific open conjecture in this exact area: conj:qou-infra-discharges-goncharov-zeta5 proposes discharging the depth-3 motivic conjecture at Q(zeta_5), and its stated second route is to express the 22-term relation restricted to fifth roots of unity as an explicit element and kill it by Hecke normal-form reduction. Relations among Li_3 at roots of unity are what the shuffle machinery in Chapter 2 produces. Honest limits, and the reason this is not core: the thesis does not supply the 22-term relation at zeta_5, works mainly in weight <= 4, and I have not verified that its shuffle relations restrict usefully to fifth-root arguments. It is a technique source for an open conjecture, and should be cited as such rather than as a discharge.

keyResults.statement: General families of double shuffle relations on Hodge and motivic correlators on the punctured projective line, together with the correlator-to-multiple-polylogarithm dictionary and new functional equations on the Hodge correlator integrals.
keyResults.useForFolio: The relation-generating machinery the second route of conj:qou-infra-discharges-goncharov-zeta5 needs; also relevant to prop:depth-2-identification-bloch-suslin as the weight-3 continuation of the depth-2 story.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; the folio has an open conjecture explicitly in the depth-3 motivic programme at Q(zeta_5) and no registered source for the shuffle-relation machinery it proposes to use.

Before this is used for anything stronger, someone must check whether the double shuffle relations here actually restrict to fifth-root-of-unity arguments in weight 3 and generate relations independent of the multiplication formula the conjecture already quotients by. I did not verify that, so aid-proof would be an over-claim.

relevance.rationale: A long review of the Magnus expansion: representing the solution of a linear system with varying coefficients as a single exponential of a series of nested commutators, with existence and convergence theorems, an improved radius of convergence, the relation to BCH, the Fer and Wei-Norman product alternatives, and the connection to the Chen-Fliess series. The folio's mass identity is the norm of a nonabelian multiplicative integral (Yekutieli), and prop:mi-sw-abelianisation's authorNotes record that no Lean instance is expected because the construction needs nonabelian gauge theory and Yekutieli multiplicative integration -- so a computable, convergence-controlled representation of a path-ordered product is squarely on the folio's critical path. Supporting rather than core, for a specific reason: the corpus's MI is SURFACE-ordered (an integral over an exceptional divisor, requiring nonabelian Stokes), whereas Magnus is the theory of the path-ordered (one-dimensional) case, which this review does not extend to surface ordering. So it supplies technique for a sub-problem, not for the stated object. Corpus-grep over content/, docs/, computations/: no Magnus, Fer, BCH or Chen-Fliess material exists anywhere, so this is an absence rather than a duplicate.

keyResults.statement: Existence of the Magnus exponent and convergence of the Magnus series, with an improved radius of convergence in terms of the integrated operator norm.
keyResults.useForFolio: A proved convergence criterion for the exponential representation of a path-ordered transport -- the kind of statement that could make a Lean-tractable sub-case of the MI machinery, in contrast to the current position that no instance is expected. What would need checking: whether the corpus's connection-curvature pair restricted to a path in the exceptional divisor satisfies the norm bound.

keyResults.locator: Sect. 3.5 (Magnus expansion and the Chen-Fliess series)
keyResults.statement: The relation between the Magnus exponent and the Chen-Fliess series of iterated integrals.
keyResults.useForFolio: Chen iterated integrals are the algebraic backbone of the shuffle Hopf algebra the corpus builds its level-2 primitive on; this is an explicit bridge between that combinatorial side and the analytic transport side, which the folio currently keeps separate.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry and no Magnus/BCH/Chen-Fliess material anywhere in the corpus, despite the mass identity being defined through a nonabelian multiplicative integral.

Record the path-ordered Magnus representation and its convergence criterion next to prop:mi-sw-abelianisation's no-instance note, stating plainly that Magnus covers the one-dimensional case only and that the surface-ordered case the corpus needs is not addressed here. relevance.rationale: Defines a TWISTED version of the Neumann--Zagier matrices of an ideal triangulation, establishes their symplectic properties, and shows how to compute them from the combinatorics of the triangulation; as an application it defines a twisted one-loop invariant which determines the one-loop invariant of the cyclic covers of a hyperbolic knot complement and is conjecturally the adjoint twisted Alexander polynomial. The corpus depends on NZ matrices heavily and got one wrong. computations/probes/borromean_nz_adjoint_torsion.py carries a correction banner dated 2026-08-07 stating that its determinant is 'the WRONG construction', that its 4_1 calibration of sqrt(3) is exactly twice the correct value, and that its |det J_NZ(B_3)| = 64 'is not an invariant' because it varies under retriangulation and framing. The same arc's audit says the multi-cusp derivation 'is not in DG at all', i.e. the corpus went looking for literature covering its case and did not find this paper. A systematic treatment of NZ matrices computed directly from triangulation combinatorics is exactly what a construction that just failed retriangulation-invariance needs. One scoping limit must be respected and stated: the twisted one-loop invariant here is defined for ONE-CUSPED hyperbolic 3-manifolds. That covers the corpus's 4_1 calibration, which is where the factor-of-two error was found, but it does NOT cover the three-cusped Borromean complement, so this document must not be cited as settling the multi-cusp case. Corpus-grep run: no ref() entry for it (checked by author and by DOI stem; the neighbouring 2023 entry in the same journal is a different paper), and no audit or coordination ledger mentions twisted NZ matrices.

keyResults.statement: Twisted Neumann--Zagier matrices are defined, shown to retain the symplectic properties of the untwisted ones, and computed directly from the combinatorics of an ideal triangulation.
keyResults.useForFolio: The reference construction against which the corpus's corrected NZ determinant should be checked, in a form that is explicitly combinatorial and therefore testable for the retriangulation invariance the corpus's earlier version failed.

relevance.rationale: Proves that a slight modification of the Burau representation of the braid group is unitary with respect to an explicitly constructed Hermitian form: there is a nonsingular (n-1)x(n-1) matrix J_0 over Z[t, t^{-1}] with beta(w)* J_0 beta(w) = J_0 for every braid word, becoming genuinely Hermitian after passing to Z[s, s^{-1}] with s^2 = t, and each standard generator acts as a unitary reflection. Two corpus places touch this. First, the T2 layer computes explicit Burau-at-i matrices and QOU/Machinery/HeckeMonodromyJordan.lean proves the monodromy is non-semisimple there ((sigma - i)^2 = 0, eigenvalues colliding at q = i), where the behaviour of an invariant Hermitian form is exactly the sort of structure that governs whether a Jordan block can appear. Second, q-game-of-life-proof asserts flatly that 'each generator is unitary with respect to the Markov trace form' with no citation. Supporting rather than core, for an honest reason: the form proved invariant here is J_0 on the reduced Burau module, which is NOT the same object as the Markov trace form on H_n(q) that the corpus's unitarity claim names, and no corpus derivation currently consumes an invariant Hermitian form. It is the right literature to cite and the right thing to check against, not a discharge.

keyResults.statement: There is a nonsingular matrix J_0 over Z[t,t^{-1}] with beta(w)* J_0 beta(w) = J_0 for all braid words; over Z[s,s^{-1}] (s^2 = t) a change of basis makes it Hermitian, and each generator acts as a unitary reflection.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the standard invariant-form statement for the braid representation the corpus's Burau-at-i computation uses, and a citable anchor for the corpus's otherwise unsourced unitarity assertion.

Deliberately not proposed as aid-proof: the Jordan-block proof is already sorry-free and does not need this, and the two forms have not been reconciled.
