relevance.rationale: Garoufalidis-Kashaev, 'From state integrals to q-series': a detailed proof, for a family of one-dimensional state integrals I_{A,B}(b) = int Phi_b(x)^B exp(-A pi i x^2) dx, that such integrals equal finite sums of products of a q-series and a q-tilde-series, with q = exp(2 pi i b^2) and q-tilde = exp(-2 pi i / b^2); the mechanism is the factorized structure of Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm Phi_b = (e^{2 pi b(x+c_b)}; q)_infty / (e^{2 pi b^{-1}(x-c_b)}; q-tilde)_infty together with its pole structure and the residue theorem, and the worked applications are the state-integral invariants of the 4_1 and 5_2 knots. That factorization IS the object the corpus's live c_3 bar-odd front is built on: docs/audits/2026-07-25-5two-gk-bridge-attack.md (beans qou-reat, o3cv, jtii, exes) works entirely with 'the GK bilinear block pairing Z = sum M_{sigma sigma'} B_sigma(q) B-tilde_{sigma'}(q-tilde)' and its state-integral dressing, and the corpus's registered sources for it are GK 1411.6062 (evaluation at rational points) and GGM (peacock patterns) -- the theorem that produces the bilinear q / q-tilde block form in the first place has no ref() entry, and both of its worked knots are exactly the corpus's two.

keyResults.statement: The one-dimensional state integral I_{A,B}(b) equals a finite sum of products of a q-series and a q-tilde-series, obtained by residues from the factorized form of Phi_b, with generating series F_{A,B}(q,x).
keyResults.useForFolio: The theorem that licenses the bilinear block form Z = sum M B_sigma(q) B-tilde_{sigma'}(q-tilde) on which the 5_2 GK-bridge attack's 440 pre-registered entry comparisons and its block-row-selection successor are built; currently used with no citation for the factorization itself.

relevance.rationale: WRONG JOIN — REPORT LOUDLY. This row was seeded to 'kirillov1995', whose registered entry is a single-author article on dilogarithm identities in a theoretical-physics supplement series. The attached file is a different author's book-length survey of the dilogarithm function, whose table of contents runs: I. the dilogarithm in geometry and number theory (special values; functional equations; the Bloch-Wigner function D(z) and its generalizations; volumes of hyperbolic 3-manifolds; values of Dedekind zeta functions), II. further aspects (variants of the dilogarithm; dilogarithm identities; dilogarithms and modular functions and the Nahm equation; higher polylogarithms). No id for this survey exists in content/schema/references.ts (searched by author, by subject and by title words; the nearest same-author entry is a different text on hyperbolic manifolds and Dedekind zeta values), so id is set to null. RELEVANCE OF THE DOCUMENT IS HIGH: the Bloch-Wigner function, volumes of hyperbolic 3-manifolds, Dedekind zeta special values and the Nahm equation are all live QOU topics, and the corpus runs recurring Bloch-Wigner and hyperbolic-volume arguments. CONSEQUENT FLAG ON THE 'kirillov1995' CITATIONS, which I could not verify because the attached file is not that work: lean/QOU/BraidKnot/Li2qUniqueness.lean cites the id at three distinct locators — section 2.1 for the truncated symmetric q-dilogarithm sum z^n/(n [n]_q) with symmetric q-integers (line 31), 'Proposition 2.1' for the Briggs-Klein integral identity (line 62), and 'Proposition 2.3' for antiderivative uniqueness from the fundamental theorem of calculus (line 67). The integral homology action the second site needs is developed in §2 (the induced matrix [f]_* on H_1(B,Z) in a canonical basis built from the 20-sided hyperbolic polygon), and the phrase 'entries 0, +-1' does not occur in the text. relevance.rationale: Identified from front matter as arXiv:math/0005296v1 (math.QA, 31 May 2000) by Bang-He Li and Tian-Jun Li, a three-page note exhibiting two lens spaces to show that Ohtsuki's tau for rational homology spheres does not determine the full family of Kirby-Melvin SO(3) invariants {tau'_r, r odd >= 3}. Same subject area as the rest of this cohort — perturbative versus root-of-unity quantum 3-manifold invariants — but scope-(a): this document, as read, supplies nothing this folio can use. The reason is precise rather than impressionistic. The counterexample is s(6,25) = s(11,25), giving tau(L(25,11)) = tau(L(25,6)) while xi_r differs exactly when (r,25) is not 1; every branch of its formula (1) that produces a discrepancy requires c = gcd(p,r) > 1, hence |H_1(M,Z)| > 1. The corpus's only 3-manifold is the INTEGRAL homology sphere Sigma(2,3,5) (|H_1| = 0), where the c = 1 branch applies and the determination theorem the paper itself cites — Rozansky's proof of Lawrence's conjecture, i.e. the sibling document library/arxiv-q-alg-9504015v2/9504015v2.pdf — holds. So the obstruction is vacuous here. Independently, a grep of content/**/*.md for 'lens space' returns nothing: the corpus has no lens-space content for this to bear on. Citation status checked all three ways: no ref() id among the 481 registered (no Li, no Kirby-Melvin, no Ohtsuki lambda_n entry), no cite{} in content/**/*.md, no '-- Ref:' in content/**/*.lean, and a grep for '0005296' across the tree returns only the ledger row. Recording no key results, per the skill's rule that an empty list is the honest outcome when no named place here wants them; the verdict is not that the technique is excluded, only that this document supplies nothing usable at present. Should the corpus ever acquire a rational-homology-sphere object with non-trivial H_1, this note becomes the sharp statement of where the perturbative series stops determining the root-of-unity data, and the verdict should be revisited.

keyResults.useForFolio: Independently confirms the support set {1,11,19,29} that computations/probes/keystone_colored_sigma235_wrt.py hardcodes, and simultaneously pins the exponent normalisation as (n^2-1)/120 — which makes every exponent an integer (n=1,11,19,29 give 0,1,3,7) — whereas that probe uses Psi(q) = sum chi(n) q^{n^2/120}. The two differ by an overall q^{-1/120}; at the probe's evaluation point that is a factor ~1.00088, i.e. it moves the operational number Psi(1/q0) = 2.32958 in its fourth significant digit. This is a normalisation cross-check to run, not a number to adopt.

keyResults.statement: Defines the slope sigma(M) = lim_{n->inf} lambda_n(M) / (n lambda_{n-1}(M)); cites Lawrence-Rozansky that the slope exists for Seifert fibred manifolds and equals sigma(Sigma(Q_1/P_1,...,Q_N/P_N)) = ±P/pi^2 = ±(1/pi^2)(sum_i Q_i/P_i)^{-1}, so pi^2 sigma(M) is in Q for such manifolds and in Z when they are additionally integer homology spheres.
keyResults.useForFolio: For Sigma(2,3,5) both readings of P give |pi^2 sigma| = 30 = p1 p2 p3, the same 30 the keystone's McKay 2I <-> affine E8 derivation uses as h(E8) = sum of Coxeter marks (docs/coordination/s5-so3-keystone.md, 2026-07-12 row). So the growth rate of the perturbative coefficients is that same P: lambda_n grows like (30/pi^2)^n n!, i.e. Z_inf(Sigma(2,3,5)) is Gevrey-1 with zero radius of convergence. That is a quantitative reason why the keystone's h = q-1 expansion cannot simply be evaluated at the substrate (h_0 ~ 0.11) and why the bar-involution route into the disk (q -> 1/q, where the false theta converges) is the correct one — it corroborates a route the ledger already chose, and supplies the divergence rate the ledger currently does not record.

keyResults.statement: The b-6j symbol has b -> 0 saddle-point asymptotics exp(W_pm(A)/(2 pi i b^2)) with W_pm(A) = U(z_pm, A) + Delta(A) - (5/3) pi^2 -+ 2 pi^2 phi, whose imaginary part is the tetrahedron-volume formula (3.3) quoted from its ref [MY, Thm 2]; the potential U(u, A) is an alternating sum of eight dilogarithms in the dihedral-angle variables A_k = exp(i eta_k), and the saddles are the two roots of dU/du = -2 pi i / u.

relevance.rationale: Identified from front matter (hep-th preprint, v2). No ref() entry, no \cite{} site in content/**/*.md, no -- Ref: in content/**/*.lean; the arXiv id appears nowhere in content/ -> orphan on all three checks. Its Section 4 is the figure-eight (4_1) Andersen-Kashaev state integral written explicitly as a lateral Borel resummation of a trans-series, i.e. the QOU muon anchor. What it supplies that the corpus does not already have from `fantini-wheeler2024`: that reference proves Borel summability of the *perturbative* series; this document addresses the SECOND stage -- after each sector is Borel resummed, the trans-series is still an infinite sum over exponentially small corrections, which is a potential new divergence (the so-called divergence of the OPE). def:ecalle-borel-resummation stops at the single-series median sum and rem:st-is-median-resummation then asserts st = L^med for a *transseries*, so the corpus is currently silently assuming exactly the premise this document isolates. Epistemic scope, stated honestly: this is not a theorem-numbered result. For complex Chern-Simons (Sec 4) the convergence is DERIVED from exact expressions for M_1, M_2 that the document itself attributes as conjectural to its ref [41] (the GGM resurgent-structure paper, arXiv:2007.10190); for the integrable models (Sec 5) it is numerical evidence. Its eq (4.5) coefficients were cross-checked here against the q-series already self-checked in computations/probes/fourone_stokes_series_selfcheck.py and reproduce them exactly (see keyResults), which is what raises this from supporting to core: there is a concrete, named script that should carry the check.

keyResults.statement: The Borel-resummed trans-series s_pm(Phi) = sum_l y^l s_pm(phi_l)(g) is itself an infinite sum over non-perturbative sectors and is a potential new source of divergence; reorganising by fixed power n of the coupling gives the partial series G_n(y) = sum_l a_{n,l} y^l, and convergence of the G_n with a common radius R (eq 2.8) is the property that makes the resummed trans-series a well-defined function.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the second-stage premise that def:ecalle-borel-resummation does not define and rem:st-is-median-resummation silently uses. That remark identifies st(f~|_eps) with L^med(f~) for a transseries f~, citing Watson/Nevanlinna-Sokal uniqueness -- which is a one-series statement. The sum over sectors is a separate convergence question, and this gives the vocabulary (partial series, common radius R) to state it.

keyResults.statement: For the figure-eight complement the Andersen-Kashaev invariant I(tau) is written as a lateral Borel resummation of an explicit trans-series with two complex-instanton towers q~^l exp(-+ V/(2 pi tau)), q~ = exp(-2 pi i / tau), V = 2.029883... the hyperbolic volume, with perturbative series phi_g(tau) = 3^{-1/4}(1 + ...) and phi_c(tau) = phi_g(-tau); the partial series factorise as G^i_n(y) = a_n M_i(y), so the radius-1 convergence of M_{1,2} gives convergence of every partial series, with the same radius for all n.
keyResults.useForFolio: The 4_1 instance of the previous item, at the corpus's own muon anchor and with V = Vol(4_1) as the instanton action. The corpus has a 5_2 analogue (computations/probes/qbeta_5two_median_borel_resummation_probe.py, which records that the substrate ray misses every Stokes ray) but no 4_1 counterpart; this is the published trans-series a 4_1 probe would be written against.

Verified during this triage by exact rational power-series arithmetic: M_1 = g_0 * 2G_0 exactly through the printed order q^4 (product coefficients 1, -8, -9, 18, 46 reproduce eq (4.5) term by term). M_2 has no comparable factorisation at this order: M_2/g_0 = -9q - 12q^2 + 9q^3 + 36q^4, M_2/(g_0 * 2G_0) = -9q - 75q^2 - 642q^3 - 5580q^4. Scope: 4 non-trivial coefficients matched, which is evidence of the identity, not a proof of it.

So it neither proves nor refutes the statement the corpus over-claims. What it does supply is (i) a clean, quotable separation of the convergent-q-series layer from the Borel/resurgent layer, which rem:channel-rotation-askey-lit item 3 currently runs together, and (ii) a calibration datum on the BPS identification (see keyResults). relevance.rationale: Identified from front matter (math.GT, v1). No ref() entry, no \cite{} site, no Lean -- Ref:; arXiv id absent from content/ -> orphan on all three checks. Content: its Theorem 1.2 gives a full asymptotic expansion of the Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant RT_r(M_{p,q}) of the closed hyperbolic 3-manifold obtained by integral q-surgery along the twist knot K_p, at the root of unity exp(4 pi i / r) with r odd, including the exponential term exp((N + 1/2) zeta(p,q)) whose critical value is the complex volume, a one-loop prefactor omega(p,q) built from the Hessian H(p,q; z_1, z_2, z_3), and all higher corrections kappa_i(p,q)/r^i -- thereby proving the RT form of the volume conjecture for that family. HYPOTHESIS CHECK, which is why this is tangential rather than supporting: the theorem holds only for (p,q) in the set S of eq (1.2), whose condition (1.3) requires p >= 6 (with q >= 12..27 depending on p). Its own Sec 3 states K_{-1} = 4_1, K_1 = 3_1, K_2 = 5_2. So the two knots the corpus actually anchors on -- 4_1 (muon anchor) and 5_2 (saddle source) -- are BOTH outside the admissible set, and its Sec 1 attributes the figure-eight surgery cases to other authors (its refs [18] and [23]). Supporting rather than core: it supplies the machinery and the literature warrant for reading a perturbative Chern-Simons expansion as the Ohtsuki series, which is the framing the keystone's Beasley-Witten localization route assumes, but the corpus consumes no result of this paper today and none of its statements discharges a named obligation. keyResults.statement: Ohtsuki's invariants lambda_n(M) and the loop corrections S_n(M) to the trivial-connection contribution determine each other through sum_n lambda_n(M) x^n = exp[ sum_{n>=1} (S_n(M) - S_n(S^3)) (i pi/K)^n ] evaluated at x = exp(2 pi i/K) - 1, with S_1(M) = 6 lambda_CW.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the keystone's Chern-Simons framing its literature warrant at exactly the manifold class it needs: the identification is verified in Section 4 for Seifert manifolds, the class containing S^3/2I = Sigma(2,3,5). It says the perturbative expansion of a localized CS partition function on that manifold is the exponential of the connected loop corrections whose resummation is the Ohtsuki series — the step the Beasley-Witten route (#2524) takes for granted.

keyResults.statement: The Kirby-Melvin surgery formula for Z'(M;k) as a sum over odd colours of the framing-independent coloured Jones polynomial weighted by prod_j sin(pi alpha_j/K); and, for the Seifert surgery link of N unknots linked to a single unknot, the explicit sine-product coloured Jones J_{beta,alpha_1..alpha_N}(L;k) = prod_j sin(pi beta alpha_j/K) / [sin^{N-1}(pi beta/K) sin(pi/K)] up to normalisation.
keyResults.useForFolio: The per-colour weight sin(pi alpha/K) is the S-matrix vacuum row d_alpha/D that KeystoneRTSurgeryConstruction.lean proves the RT surgery sum weights each label by — so (1.6) is an explicit analytic instance of the assembly that file formalises abstractly. Equation (4.28) then gives the coloured Seifert link invariant in closed sine-product form, which is the machinery the colored-Sigma(2,3,5) step needs to lift the bare closed-manifold number to a lambda-indexed family. Useful as a cited construction to build against; it is not a substitute for the carried (RT) hypothesis.

relevance.rationale: FALSE FRIEND — the 'q' in the filename is NOT the substrate deformation parameter. relevance.rationale: IDENTIFICATION FINDING: the filename says 'Ohtsuki-99' but the front matter identifies a 1999 Acta Mathematica Sinica (English Series) 15(3) 293-316 article by Xiaosong Lin and Zhenghan Wang, ON Ohtsuki's invariants — Ohtsuki is the subject, not an author. keyResults.statement: If M is the Poincare homology 3-sphere Sigma(2,3,5), realised as +1-surgery on the right-handed trefoil, then lambda_2(M) = 39. (Companion: Sigma(2,3,7) from +1-surgery on the left-handed trefoil has lambda_2 = 63.)
keyResults.useForFolio: A parameter-free external number for the second Ohtsuki coefficient of S^3/2I. Expanding the corpus's Sigma(2,3,5) false theta in h = q-1 must reproduce it (together with lambda_1 = 6 lambda_Casson = ±6, the trefoil having a_2 = 1). This is the falsifiable check the keystone transcription lacks. Caveat that must be settled before the comparison means anything: Lin-Wang's orientation is +1-surgery on the RIGHT-handed trefoil, and their own Remark on the same page gives lambda_2(Mbar) = lambda_2(M) + lambda_1(M) under orientation reversal — so the corpus's orientation convention has to be fixed first, or the check will fail for a bookkeeping reason rather than a mathematical one.

keyResults.locator: Theorem 1.1 (p. 293) and Corollary 5.1 (p. 303), strengthened at Theorem 7.1

keyResults.useForFolio: An integrality sieve on any lambda_n the corpus extracts from its own Sigma(2,3,5) series: a transcription that yields a non-integer, or an integer not divisible by 3 at n=2, is wrong independently of any numerical tolerance. Cheap, exact, and it fails loudly — the right kind of gate for a transcription check. Consistent with the quoted value (39 = 3 x 13).

keyResults.statement: Explicit surgery formulae expressing lambda_1 and lambda_2 of a manifold obtained by Dehn surgery on a unit-framed algebraically split link as sums over sublinks; specialised to 1/n-surgery on a knot K these express lambda_2 through Vassiliev invariants read off the Conway and Jones polynomials of K, and give lambda_2(M)/3 = mu(M) mod 2 with mu the Rokhlin invariant.

Two independent in-corpus computations of the same lambda_2 would make the check self-contained rather than dependent on a quoted literature value.

relevance.rationale: READ VIA PAGE IMAGES (pdftoppm at 90-110 dpi; the PDF is an image-only scan, pdftotext yields ~18 chars), 18 pages, front matter and running heads legible. Subject: meromorphic solutions of the NONLINEAR ORDINARY difference equation y(x+1) = R(x, y(x)) with R = P/Q rational in y (eqs. 1.1-1.4), q_0 := max(deg P, deg Q) (eq. 1.5). Thm 1 (p. 311): a transcendental meromorphic solution has Nevanlinna characteristic T(r, y) >= K_1((1-eps) q_0)^r, hence order infinity unless q_0 = 1 — proved from Valiron's theorem T(r, R(x,y)) = q_0 T(r,y) + O(log r). Thm 3 (p. 313): a Picard-type value-distribution trichotomy driven by 'maximally fixed values / pairs' of R. Sec. 3 (p. 315) + Cor. 6: existence of meromorphic solutions for any rational R, with asymptotic expansions in x^{-1/m} carrying (log x / x)^k corrections, valid in the sectors D_1(R, eps); Sec. 4 (pp. 315-320) gives asymptotic behaviour in horizontal strips Sigma(eta; A, alpha) via Lemmas 14-16. DIRECT ANSWER TO THE QUESTION POSED: this is NOT the corpus's problem class, merely adjacent. Two mismatches, either one decisive. (1) OPERATOR: Yanagihara's is the ADDITIVE shift x -> x+1; the corpus's C1 object is the q-DILATION sigma acting through L1 = (q^2 x - 1) sigma^2 - (q-1) sigma - (q-1) (docs/audits/2026-08-08-rsz-c1-infinity-route-closed.md), and sec:q-difference-viewpoint-method defines the folio's shift as sigma_q : q -> q zeta. (2) LINEARITY: Yanagihara's equation is nonlinear in y (that is the whole point — the Nevanlinna machinery exists to handle R(x,y) rational in y); the corpus's C1 operator is linear. Note also a notation trap: Yanagihara's 'q_0' (eq. 1.5) is max(deg P, deg Q), an integer degree, and has nothing to do with the substrate q_0 ~ 1.10998. On the C1 degree-budget question specifically: the growth Yanagihara controls is the Nevanlinna characteristic T(r, y) of a SOLUTION in the complex plane, not the q-degree of the COEFFICIENTS of a formal series; the corpus's budget is deg_q(c_n) = n^2 against the q-Borel kernel exponent, a different quantity for a different object, and the paper contains no Borel/q-Borel transform, no summability level, no slope filtration and no Stokes multipliers. Citation status checked three ways: no ref() entry (an author-surname grep over content/schema/references.ts returns empty), no \cite site in content/**/*.md, no '-- Ref:' in content/**/*.lean; the corpus's only Nevanlinna hits are the unrelated Nevanlinna-Sokal Borel-summability criterion and the Nevanlinna parametrization of indeterminate moment problems. Scope-(a) negative: this document, as read, supplies nothing usable for the C1 infinity-residual; it is not a claim that difference-equation value-distribution theory is excluded from the folio.

If the folio ever needs value-distribution growth bounds it should look for the q-difference Nevanlinna literature instead, not this additive-shift paper.

relevance.rationale: Groebner-Shirshov bases for Coxeter GROUPS W = sgp<Sigma | (s s')^m = 1>. It is supporting rather than tangential because it lands on a named, live piece of folio machinery: the Groebner-Shirshov warrant for H_n(q). Two things it supplies. (1) Example 3.2 (pp. 4-5) refutes by explicit counterexample the Bokut-Shiao conjecture that a GS basis of an arbitrary Coxeter group is obtainable from S = {(1),(2),(3')} using only the commuting relations, and its introduction restricts the known positive results to FINITE Coxeter groups; type A_{n-1} is finite, so the folio's own case is untouched, and recording that is the point so nobody later invokes 'GS bases for Coxeter groups' generically. (2) Its bibliography, entry [4] on p. 21, supplies the coordinates for the refid [bokut2001], which was cited at QOU/Archimedean/MassGapGm.lean:46 and named in the References block of UGB/GrobnerShirshov/HeckeGS.lean with no entry in references.ts; that entry was created in the same commit as this row, from three agreeing bibliographies in this batch. WRITER CORRECTION to the triage that produced this row: it described a live axiom hecke_is_gs_basis at HeckeGS.lean:153-158, justified in an axiom-budget table as 'Bokut & Shiao 2001, Thm 3.5' and carrying an inline '-- Ref: [bokutchen2014]'. On this branch that axiom does NOT exist. It was deleted as FALSE, and NotAGSBasis.hecke_not_gs_basis_four machine-refutes it at n = 4; the module header says so and names the missing Bokut-Shiao completion family sigma_i sigma_{i-1} ... sigma_j sigma_i -> sigma_{i-1} sigma_i sigma_{i-1} ... sigma_j. The document's value survives the correction and sharpens: the live consumer is bean qou-auq3 (complete the system), and the scope note belongs there. What this document does NOT do, and why it is not core: it proves nothing about H_n(q), never mentions a deformation parameter, and so cannot license the transfer from C[W] to the Hecke algebra that qou-auq3 needs. Scope-(a) negative: as read, it supplies no lemma that closes a gap in the folio's own argument; its value is scoping and bibliographic hygiene.

keyResults.statement: S = {(1),(2),(3')} is a Groebner-Shirshov basis of W whenever no f in (3') has any of the four inclusion-composition properties C1-C4; three explicit families of Coxeter matrices satisfy this, including (i) all m_ij >= 3 for i > j.
keyResults.useForFolio: Unconditional, non-finiteness-based warrant for the q=1 shadow of the smallest case: the rank-2 matrix m12 = 3 (W = S_3, whose six elements index the normal forms of def:hecke-normal-form) satisfies (i). For n >= 4 none of the three families applies (m_13 = 2 kills (i) and (ii), m_21 = 3 kills (iii)), so there the warrant reverts to the finite-type theorem. Either way this is W, not H_n(q), and any remark must say so.

relevance.rationale: A 13-page survey of Groebner-Shirshov / Composition-Diamond machinery organised around eight PBW theorems; it proves nothing new, and a full-text keyword scan returns zero hits for Hecke, Temperley, Iwahori, Catalan, Young and quantum group, so it bears on NONE of the branch's five live fronts. Its bearing is on the other chapter, unital-groebner-bases, and it is specific. Sec. 3.7 (p. 6, read and verified in the PDF) collects the counterexamples to PBW for Lie algebras over a commutative algebra: Shirshov 1953 and Cartier 1958 unconditionally, plus Cohn's 1963 family L_p = Lie_K(x1,x2,x3 | y3x3 = y2x2 + y1x1) over K = k[y1,y2,y3 | y_i^p = 0], proved for p = 2, 3, 5 by Bokut-Chen-Chen. Both folio copies of the PBW corollary -- cor:pbw and cor:ugb-pbw -- state Ug isomorphic to Sg as an R-module for a Lie algebra over an arbitrary commutative ring with unity and carry NO freeness hypothesis, while both proofs open by choosing a well-ordered basis for g (verified in the working tree: pbw-corollary.md and pbw-corollary-proof.md in unital-groebner-bases-chapter, and pbw-corollary.md in buchberger-and-pbw). Every neighbouring block in that chapter states 'free as an R-module' explicitly, so the omission reads as a drafting slip. Cohn's K is a commutative ring with unity and L_p is not K-free, so the counterexample family sits inside the corollary's stated hypotheses, and a module isomorphism compatible with the canonical map would force g -> Ug injective. Graded supporting rather than core because the document is a secondary source: it reports the counterexamples in one paragraph and proves none of them, so the primary citations belong to Cartier 1958 / Shirshov 1953 / Bokut-Chen-Chen 2011, none of which is in references.ts or has been read. It supplies nothing toward the one open sorry in the PBW Lean files (normal_form_exists, the termination half), so no aid-proof is proposed.

keyResults.statement: Shirshov (1953) and Cartier (1958) give counterexamples to PBW for Lie algebras over a commutative algebra; Cohn (1963) conjectures that L_p = Lie_K(x1,x2,x3 | y3x3 = y2x2 + y1x1) over K = k[y1,y2,y3 | y_i^p = 0] does not embed into its universal enveloping associative algebra, and Bokut-Chen-Chen prove the conjecture for p = 2, 3, 5.
keyResults.useForFolio: Names the counterexamples showing the missing 'free as an R-module' hypothesis in cor:pbw / cor:ugb-pbw cannot simply be dropped, and supplies the citation for both the hypothesis fix and a sharpness remark.

keyResults.statement: For L = Lie_k(X|S) with U(L) = k<X | S^(-)>: S is a Lie GS basis iff S is an associative GS basis, and in that case U(L) has linear basis {u_1 ... u_t : u_1 <= ... <= u_t, u_i in Irr(S) intersect ALSW(X)}.
keyResults.useForFolio: prf:pbw asserts 'the argument that G is a Groebner-Shirshov basis is exactly as in the classical setting' and cites nothing at all (pbw-corollary-proof.ts has no cites field). This is the classical field-case statement that sentence defers to.

keyResults.statement: Over a commutative algebra K one works in the double-free algebra M_{k[Y]}(X) with lcm(u_Y u_X, v_Y v_X) = lcm(u_Y,v_Y) lcm(u_X,v_X); a composition relative to a trivial lcm(u_X,v_X) is automatically trivial over a field but NOT over a commutative algebra when lcm(u_Y,v_Y) != u_Y v_Y, so a given pair generally has infinitely many compositions.
keyResults.useForFolio: Candidate one-line remark on why the commutative ground ring costs this chapter nothing -- the folio requires unit leading coefficients (LC in R^x, lambda in R^*) plus a monomial basis, so coefficients never entangle with the word monoid. GATED: it must first be checked that those unit conditions genuinely exclude the non-trivial trivial-lcm compositions rather than merely making them unreachable in the worked examples.

proposedActions.rationale: cor:pbw states the isomorphism over an arbitrary commutative ring with unity with no hypothesis on g, but its proof begins 'Choose a well-ordered basis {x_i | i in I} for g'. Add 'which is free as an R-module' to the statement, matching the wording every other block in the chapter uses, and cite Sec. 3.7 for why it cannot be dropped. The joined bean covers both copies plus the Lean docstrings.

Same defect in the second copy: buchberger-and-pbw/pbw-corollary.md states the corollary with no freeness hypothesis and then proves it by 'Choosing a well-ordered basis {x_i | i in I} for g'. Fix both copies in one change so they do not drift apart.

A sharpness remark recording that the freeness hypothesis is not cosmetic: over a commutative ring PBW genuinely fails, and Cohn's family is the standard witness. Must be phrased as reported-by-survey unless the primaries are read first; none of Cohn, Cartier, Shirshov or Bokut-Chen-Chen is in references.ts.

One-line remark on why the commutative ground ring costs nothing here, gated on the check named in the third keyResult. Drop the remark if the check fails -- in which case thm:buchberger has a defect and needs its own item.

relevance.rationale: VERDICT CHANGED BY THE WRITER from supporting to tangential, on evidence the single-document pass could not have: this is the arXiv sibling of the published document assessed at library/fd58d8e182edda805fed0946606c5ab82f81/fd58d8e182edda805fed0946606c5ab82f81.pdf (registered as kimlee2018), by the same two authors in the same year, and its Sec. 3 -- the only folio-relevant part of either -- is VERBATIM the same type A_{n-1} review, down to Prop. 3.1, the monomial order, the standard-monomial description and Example 3.2 with |M_{T(A_3)}| = C_4 = 14. Both quote that proposition from Kang-Lee-Lee-Oh, J. Algebra 252 (2002) Prop. 6.2. The two documents differ only in their own theorems: the published one does type B, this one does types B and D (dim T(B_n) = (n+2)C_n - 1, dim T(D_n) = ((n+3)/2)C_n - 1), and the folio is strictly type A -- corpus-grep for 'Coxeter type', 'type B_n', 'type D_n' over content/ returns nothing outside .lake. So this document contributes no citable content the published sibling does not already carry, and registering it would create a bibliography entry with no load-bearing citation site. Tangential is the honest verdict on THIS row and it should be read together with the kimlee2018 row rather than as a judgement on the mathematics, which is identical. The Sec. 3 content that does matter to the folio -- dim TL_n = Catalan(n) from an explicit standard-monomial basis, and the convention check that the loop parameter enters only through E_i^2 = delta E_i with E_iE_jE_i = E_i un-rescaled and delta a free complex parameter -- is recorded on the kimlee2018 row and now cited from there. A reviewer who wants type D in the bibliography should register this separately and say what cites it; do not register it unattached.

relevance.rationale: Groebner-Shirshov bases and standard-monomial bases for the GROUP ALGEBRAS C[W] of the NON-crystallographic Coxeter groups of type H: H2 = I2(5) (Prop 3.1, 10 monomials), H3 the full icosahedral group (Thm 3.3, 10 x 12 = 120 = |H3|), and H4 (Thm 4.17, 10 x 12 x 120 = 14400 = |H4|), certified by counting standard monomials against |W| or by closure under composition. The folio's Groebner-Shirshov thread is large and real, but every instance is TYPE A and q-DEFORMED: H_n(q) with sigma_i^2 -> (q - q^-1) sigma_i + 1, whose normal forms index S_n. Type H appears nowhere in content/: '600-cell', '120-cell', 'noncrystallographic', 'non-crystallographic', 'Coxeter group of type H' all return zero hits outside references.ts. The tempting bridges do not survive checking. |H3| = 120 coincides with |S5| = |Aut(Bring's curve)| and with 2 x |A5|, but H3 = A5 x C2 has a centre and S5 does not, so the icosahedral A5 that conj:klein-bring-icosahedral-bridge and the Lean theorem icosahedral_235_realizable work with is not this group; and a monomial enumeration of C[H3] does not bear on a (2,3,5)-relation realizability proof, so aid-proof would fail its hypothesis check and is not proposed. The quasicrystal framing touches rem:fivefold-crystallographic-obstruction thematically, but this document proves nothing about the crystallographic restriction -- it only cites others for it. Scope-(a) negative: as read, it supplies nothing the folio consumes; that is not a claim that Groebner-Shirshov methods for Coxeter groups are irrelevant here, since the type-A member of that literature is load-bearing. What the reading did surface, and what makes it worth the row, is the dangling refid [bokut2001] cited at QOU/Archimedean/MassGapGm.lean:46 with no entry in references.ts; that entry was created in the same commit as this row from three agreeing bibliographies in this batch, including this document's. WRITER CORRECTION to the triage that produced this row: it described that refid as the justification of a live axiom hecke_is_gs_basis in HeckeGS.lean. No such axiom exists on this branch -- it was deleted as false and is machine-refuted at n = 4 by NotAGSBasis.hecke_not_gs_basis_four. The scope question the triage raised (does the Bokut-Shiao theorem cover H_n(q) or only C[W]?) is real and is now carried by beans qou-bq5e and qou-qspu.

proposedActions.rationale: rem:fivefold-crystallographic-obstruction states the crystallographic restriction (rotational order k in {1,2,3,4,6} for n = 2,3) and ties 5-fold symmetry to aperiodicity, citing only shechtman1984 -- an experimental discovery paper, not a source for the algebraic mechanism. This document's reference list names two candidates (Patera & Twarock, J. Phys. A 35 (2002) 1551-1574; Chen-Moody-Patera, Fields Inst. Monogr. 10 (1998) 135-178), neither in references.ts. SECOND-ORDER AND UNVERIFIED: the proposal comes from seeing the works cited, not from reading them. Read Patera-Twarock before adding, and drop the action if it does not support the block's claim.

No ref() entry should be created for this document itself: GS bases for type H2/H3/H4 group algebras at q = 1 have no consumer in a folio whose Coxeter/Hecke machinery is entirely type A and q-deformed. Recording the read so the row is not re-triaged.

relevance.rationale: Groebner-Shirshov bases for the finite Coxeter GROUPS of the exceptional types G2, F4, E6, E7, E8, computed by Shirshov's algorithm over K<X> under deg-lex: a re-labelled presentation of E_n (Def 3.1, p. 6), then GB(E6) (Thm 3.2, pp. 6-7), GB(E7) (Thm 3.3, p. 8), GB(E8) (Thm 3.4, p. 10), with GB(G2) and GB(F4) in Appendix A (Thms A.3, A.4, p. 12) and a remark that n = 9 in the same presentation is the affine group. Sec. 2 is textbook GS setup and adds nothing the folio does not already have via bokutchen2014. The stated contribution is completing the exceptional types after the classical A_n, B_n, D_n cases. Two independent mismatches with this folio, either decisive. (1) TYPE: every GS object here is type A -- H_n(q) on braid generators, the normal-form words spanning H_3(q), the GS confinement filtration on T_w, the plactic/crystal bridge in type A_n. This document proves nothing in type A; the A_5 relations quoted at the head of the Thm 3.2 proof are cited, not proved. (2) DEFORMATION: its object is the Coxeter group as a semigroup presentation over a field, never the Iwahori-Hecke algebra. The folio's E6/E7/E8 sightings are affine-E8 Coxeter MARKS via McKay (cyclotomic-boundary-at-keystone) and ADE labels on ALE singularities, not normal forms in W(E8); grep for 'Coxeter group of type' and 'Weyl group of E8' over content returns nothing. None of the live fronts touches an exceptional Coxeter group. One fact worth carrying forward, reported here rather than proved here (p. 2): Chen and Liu produced a counter-example to the general Bokut conjecture on GS bases of arbitrary Coxeter groups -- that document is library/arxiv-0910.0096v1/0910.0096v1.pdf in this same batch, now registered as chenliu2009, and is the primary for the caution. Scope-(a) negative: as read, this document supplies nothing this folio can consume; that is not a claim that GS bases for Coxeter groups are irrelevant here -- the type-A member of that literature is load-bearing, it is simply a different paper.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan in an adjacent literature the folio genuinely uses, but for types the folio never touches, and at q = 1. add-reference would be inflation and cite-in-block has no honest site. Recording the classification is the useful output: a future search for 'Groebner-Shirshov bases for Coxeter groups' should not re-open this file expecting the type-A source, which is [bokut2001] for the group case and, for the deformation, Kang-Lee-Lee-Oh 2002 (bean qou-qspu).

relevance.rationale: An expository survey on the edge of algebra, logic and geometry: universal algebraic geometry over algebraic systems and logical rigidity (Sec. 2.1), Plotkin's problem on Aut(End(W(X))) for free commutative/associative algebras (Sec. 2.2), nonstandard analysis (ultraproducts at an infinite prime) applied to the Belov-Kontsevich isomorphism and to Plotkin's conjecture for polynomial symplectomorphisms (Sec. 2.3), a universal Turing machine realised inside a finitely presented algebra so that nilpotency and zero-divisor problems become undecidable (Sec. 3.1), and undecidability of the embeddability problem for varieties over a characteristic-zero field via a Matiyasevich family (Sec. 3.2). Measured against what the folio needs, it supplies nothing: a full-text search finds zero occurrences of Hecke, Temperley-Lieb, Young/partition diagram, Catalan, Wenzl, meander, Gram determinant, Connes, Rieffel, Lip-norm, Kantorovich, deuteron/nuclear, Kashaev, dilogarithm or hyperbolic volume; the two 'Markov' hits are A. A. Markov's 1947 word-problem paper and an author name, not the Markov trace. Two adjacencies were checked and both fail to be load-bearing. (a) The folio's unital-Groebner-bases chapter is about UNITAL GS bases over an arbitrary commutative ground ring; Sec. 3.1 works over a field and is about algorithmic undecidability, not ground-ring generality or PBW, and the chapter's existing citations already cover the background. (b) The information-theory chapter (rem:skein-turing-machine, thm:geometry-of-incompleteness, prop:incompleteness-implies-horizon) asserts a Turing-complete braid/Skein substrate, and Thms 3.1-3.2 are a genuine algebraic instance of computation embedded in an algebra -- but the folio makes no claim about the decidability of any algebraic property of a presented algebra, so no block wants it, and this document explicitly defers those proofs ('The entire proofs can be found at [29]') to Ivanov-Pogodaev and Malev, J. Algebra 508 (2018) 575-588, which is what should be cited if that fact is ever wanted. Scope-(a) negative: as read, it supplies nothing usable here; that is not a claim that model-theoretic or undecidability methods are irrelevant to the folio in principle.

proposedActions.rationale: Nearest live hook checked: rem:skein-turing-machine encodes a Turing machine as a braid and carries no citations, and Sec. 3.1's Thms 3.1-3.2 are the closest external analogue in the corpus. But the remark claims computation-in-a-braid, not undecidability of an algebraic property, so nothing there is unsourced; and this is a survey that defers the proofs to a different paper. Citing it would register a bibliography entry whose load-bearing content lives elsewhere.

Second hook checked: the unital-Groebner-bases chapter. Sec. 3.1's noncommutative Groebner-basis material is over a field and about undecidability; it does not touch the arbitrary-commutative-ground-ring generality that thm:unital-groebner-decomposition and cor:pbw assert, which leitnerpawloski2004 already sources.

relevance.rationale: Identified from the running head and title page, not the filename (the filename is an opaque hash). A Groebner-Shirshov basis and standard monomials for the Temperley-Lieb algebra of type B_n, after a review of type A_{n-1}, with dim T(B_n) = (n+2)C_n - 1. A document about presentations and counting, not about traces, forms or specialisations, and against the folio's live fronts it supplies almost nothing: no Markov trace, no Wedderburn weights, no q-integers, no SU(2) specialisation, nothing resembling [2]^n = sum_k m_k [n-2k+1] or sum_k m_k^2 = Catalan(n); no bilinear form of any kind, hence nothing on the meander/TL Gram determinant or positive-definiteness at real delta; nothing on Lip-norms; nothing on the Young-lattice covering relation for qou-7gei; nothing nuclear. Wenzl is not cited anywhere in it, so it neither confirms nor denies the Invent. Math. 92 (1988) attribution the branch wants. What makes it supporting is Sec. 3, and it has two live homes. First, Prop. 3.1 is a published explicit linear basis and normal form for TL_n with cardinality C_n, i.e. dim TL_n = Catalan(n) at general n from the literature, at a moment when thm:jones-markov-trace asserts H_n(q)/rad = TL_n(q) and that Catalan count with an EMPTY cites list (its own title reads '(Jones, 1987)'), and when the folio's support for the general-n count is TemperleyLiebTower.lean's catalan_three/four/five checking the folio's own table against Mathlib -- internal consistency, not a source. Second, and more consequential, Prop. 3.1's basis needs TWO FAMILIES BEYOND the defining relations (E_{i,j}E_i - E_{i-2,j}E_i and E_jE_{i,j} - E_jE_{i,j+2}), i.e. the presentation must be COMPLETED before it is confluent -- which is exactly the phenomenon that makes def:hecke-normal-form's uncited assertion 'This reduction is confluent' FALSE for the folio's three-rule system, as NotAGSBasis.hecke_not_gs_basis_four machine-refutes at n = 4. Sec. 3 also serves as an external convention check: the loop parameter enters only through E_i^2 = delta E_i, the E_iE_jE_i = E_i relation is un-rescaled and delta is a free complex parameter, which is the convention the folio adopted (e_i := q - sigma_i, e_i^2 = [2]_q e_i, delta = [2]_q) with no square root. WRITER CORRECTION to the triage that produced this row: it reported the GS basis as E_i^2 - E_i, 'the idempotent normalisation in which delta does not appear'. That was a text-extraction artifact -- the delta glyph is dropped by pypdf on this PDF. The relation is E_i^2 - delta E_i, verified against the same verbatim Sec. 3 in the sibling document library/arxiv-1808.05026v1/1808.05026v1.pdf, whose text layer renders delta correctly. Two caveats keep it out of core: Prop. 3.1 is quoted from Kang-Lee-Lee-Oh, J. Algebra 252 (2002) Prop. 6.2, which is the primary and is not yet in references.ts; and dim TL_n = C_n does not by itself give the open identity sum_k m_k^2 = Catalan(n), which additionally needs semisimplicity of TL_n at delta = 2.0108969 and the two-row indexing of the Wedderburn blocks, neither of which this document states. The document's own theorem (type B) is deliberately not recorded as a key result: the folio's type-B cluster is about partition-content cancellation and folded crystals and has no site that wants a type-B TL dimension.

keyResults.statement: Under degree-lex with E_1 < ... < E_{n-1}, T(A_{n-1}) has the Groebner-Shirshov basis {E_i^2 - delta E_i; E_iE_j - E_jE_i for i > j+1; E_{i,j}E_i - E_{i-2,j}E_i for i > j; E_jE_{i,j} - E_jE_{i,j+2} for i > j} (with E_{i,j} = E_i E_{i-1} ... E_j), and its standard monomials E_{i1,j1}...E_{ip,jp} with strictly increasing i's and j's and i_k >= j_k number the nth Catalan number, so dim T(A_{n-1}) = C_n.
keyResults.useForFolio: Two uses. (a) A literature source for dim TL_n = Catalan(n) at general n, asserted uncited at thm:jones-markov-trace and at markov-trace-frobenius-selection.md:82 and supported today only by fixed-n Lean instances. (b) The basis needs two families beyond the defining relations, which is the completion phenomenon that def:hecke-normal-form's confluence claim ignores and that NotAGSBasis.hecke_not_gs_basis_four refutes at n = 4 for the Hecke system.

keyResults.locator: Sec. 3, defining relations of T(A_{n-1}), pp. 13-14
keyResults.statement: The loop parameter enters only through E_i^2 = delta E_i; the relation E_iE_jE_i = E_i for j = i +/- 1 is un-rescaled, and delta is a free complex parameter.
keyResults.useForFolio: External convention check for the notation register's delta = [2]_q = q + q^-1 ruling: the standard presentation in the literature is the one the folio adopted, with no q^{1/2} and no delta-scaling of the E_iE_jE_i relation, which is exactly the excised convention-C error the register warns against.

keyResults.statement: The product of two standard monomials of T(A_{n-1}) is again a standard monomial up to a scalar, so the multiplication table closes on the basis.
keyResults.useForFolio: The concrete multiplication rule on the 14-element TL_4 basis, needed only if the C5 / H_4 interface claim recorded as arithmetic in TemperleyLiebTower.interface_dimension_gain is ever exhibited explicitly rather than counted. Not needed today, and qou-8iru is explicit that the H_4 interface must not be fitted.

This is a defect fix, not merely a missing citation: Prop. 3.1 here shows the same completion is needed on the Temperley-Lieb quotient, and [bokut2001] names the Coxeter-side completion family. Cite only after the block is corrected, and note that the q-deformed primary is Kang-Lee-Lee-Oh 2002, not this document.

thm:jones-markov-trace has an empty cites list while asserting H_n(q)/rad = TL_n(q), that the vanishing blocks span the radical of the trace form, and that the surviving sum of dim^2 is Catalan(n); its own title names Jones 1987. jones1987 is already in references.ts and is the primary missing citation; this document's Prop. 3.1 is the secondary source for dim TL_n = Catalan(n) with an explicit basis.

Kang-Lee-Lee-Oh, J. Algebra 252 (2002) 258-292 is the source Prop. 3.1 is quoted from and, per this document's and its sibling's introductions, the paper that computes GS bases for Hecke algebras AND Temperley-Lieb algebras of type A -- i.e. the q-deformed statement that def:hecke-normal-form and bean qou-auq3 actually need and that [bokut2001] (a Coxeter-group theorem) does not supply. NOT READ: this is a lead from two bibliographies, not a triaged source. Obtain and triage before citing it as load-bearing.
